articles.title: Inside waqf land grab in Telangana: Fake NOCs, forged ORCs
articles.summary: Telangana Waqf Board warns of land grabs using fake NOCs and forged ORCs to secure approvals, register waqf land and remove it from banned lists.
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Even as the Telangana Waqf Board continues to battle large-scale encroachments on its properties, it is now facing a new threat: Fake no-objection certificates (NOCs) and forged occupancy rights certificates (ORCs) allegedly being used to grab waqf land, secure layout approvals and have properties removed from the prohibited list.According to Waqf Board officials, land grabbers are allegedly using fabricated documents purportedly issued by the board to register properties in their names, obtain approvals from agencies such as the Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA) and Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC), and even get certain properties deleted from the Section 22-A prohibited properties list.One such case involves a purported NOC in which the Waqf Board’s chief executive officer allegedly informed the Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district collector in Dec 2025 that the board had no claim over 54 acres in Survey Nos. 233 and 316 of Atmakur mandal. Waqf Board officials, however, say the document is fake.Another alleged forged NOC surfaced in connection with Survey No. 463 in Maheshwaram village of Rangareddy district. The document, dated May 2022, reportedly stated that neither a gazette notification nor a survey commissioner’s report existed for the land. The claim is significant because the Waqf Board owns nearly 560 acres in Maheshwaram mandal, where the land is now valued at thousands of crores of rupees.In another instance, 21 acres of waqf land in Kongara Khurd village was allegedly encroached upon after layouts were developed using forged ORCs. The land was projected as Inam land through the fabricated records, following which layout permissions were obtained from HMDA.The matter assumed greater significance after the ORCs were found to bear the allegedly forged signature of Bala Maya Devi, currently an IAS officer in the BC welfare department. The signature was from her tenure as a revenue divisional officer in Rangareddy district in 1998. Officials said she approached the police last year seeking an inquiry into the alleged forgery and action against those responsible.Amid a series of such cases, the Waqf Board has alerted key govt departments and agencies, including the chief commissioner of land administration, revenue department, registration and stamps department, Telangana RERA, panchayat raj department, HMDA, GHMC and municipalities. The board has cautioned them against accepting purported waqf NOCs or clearance certificates for property transactions.“The Waqf Board does not issue any NOC, clearance certificate, memo or correspondence declaring that a particular property is not a Waqf property. Neither the Waqf Act, 1995, nor the Waqf Amendment Act, 2025, provides any provision for the issuance of such NOCs. Any document claiming to be an NOC issued by the Telangana Waqf Board should be treated as ‘void’ and should not be relied upon for registration, revenue or other official purposes,” Waqf Board CEO Mohammed Asadullah told TOI.He said any department receiving such documents should immediately refer them to the Waqf Board for verification instead of acting upon them.The CEO also warned that the board would not be responsible for transactions carried out on the basis of forged NOCs or clearance certificates. Officials processing such cases without proper verification could also face accountability, he said.Sources in the govt suspect the involvement of certain former officials and influential persons in facilitating land transactions involving waqf properties, particularly in and around Maheshwaram mandal. The board owns substantial tracts of high-value land in areas including Maheshwaram, Kandukur, Boduppal, Malkajgiri and parts of Hyderabad.Waqf Board elected member Abul Fateh Syed Bandagi Badesha Quadri said irregularities were also taking place through ORCs issued in the names of individuals rather than waqf institutions.“Even in one of the judgements by Supreme Court in 1998, the court directed to incorporate necessary entries in the revenue record, i.e. the name of the religious institution alone should be entered, not the individuals’ names. This will also put an end to the irregularities,” he said.Officials said stricter scrutiny of land records, registrations and layout approvals will be crucial to preventing further loss of waqf properties through forged documentation.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. O Instituto CPFL recebe a exposição "A Grande Muralha da China", mostra interativa que convida o público a explorar um dos monumentos mais emblemáticos do mundo por meio de recursos tecnológicos e experiências sensoriais. A exposição apresenta a trajetória histórica da muralha desde sua construção, passando pelas diferentes dinastias chinesas, pela importância da Rota da Seda e pelas transformações do monumento ao longo dos séculos.

Utilizando projeções, mapas digitais, instalações interativas, conteúdos audiovisuais e experiências imersivas, a mostra oferece uma oportunidade de aproximação com aspectos históricos, culturais e simbólicos da China.

📅 Quando: até 31 de outubro. De segunda, terça, quarta e sexta-feira, das 8h às 17h; quinta-feira, das 8h às 19h; e sábado, das 10h às 16h

A exposição parte das relações entre memória, permanência e transformação, propondo uma reflexão sobre aquilo que desaparece fisicamente, mas continua existindo por meio das lembranças, dos afetos e dos registros. Com curadoria de Gim Martins, a mostra reúne obras de Gim Martins e Sara Rezende, além de trabalhos produzidos durante as edições de 2024 e 2025 do Festival Ocre.

Ao aproximar produções concebidas para galerias e trabalhos originados no espaço urbano, a exposição questiona diferentes formas de permanência da arte e convida o público a refletir sobre aquilo que deixa marcas em pessoas, objetos e lugares.

Com curadoria de Ivo Paulino Soares, a mostra investiga as relações entre observação, território, memória e imaginação.

As obras funcionam como uma síntese visual da pesquisa desenvolvida pelo artista durante seu doutorado em Artes Visuais na Unicamp, explorando paisagens reais que gradualmente se transformam em imagens poéticas e abstratas.

📅 Quando : de 5 de setembro a 24 de outubro

MITC 2026 – Mostra Internacional Totem das Cores

A MITC 2026 – Mostra Internacional Totem das Cores chega à sua quarta edição com o tema “Ciranda das cores, um sagrado abraço”. A exposição reúne 228 obras de 160 artistas de 15 estados brasileiros e 14 países, contemplando diferentes linguagens artísticas, como pintura, escultura, arte têxtil, fotografia, videoarte, gravura, bordado e colagem.

Além da mostra principal, o evento contará com uma programação especial gratuita entre os dias 3 e 6 de setembro, incluindo palestras, rodas de conversa, performances, oficinas de cerâmica e arte têxtil, dança circular, cortejo da Congada de São Benedito e Divino Espírito Santo, homenagens e visita guiada com artistas participantes.

articles.title: Justiça de SP permite que cassino online continue em operação até 25 de outubro mesmo após MP de Lula ter vetado bets | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão não suspende integralmente medida provisória do governo Lula nem garante funcionamento da plataforma Stake até 2029; empresa terá de manter mecanismos de proteção aos apostadores e fica proibida de fazer novas campanhas e bônus.
articles.summary: Decisão não suspende integralmente medida provisória do governo Lula nem garante funcionamento da plataforma Stake até 2029; empresa terá de manter mecanismos de proteção aos apostadores e fica proibida de fazer novas campanhas e bônus.
articles.body:
Apostas online. — Foto: Joédson Alves/Agência Brasil

A Justiça Federal de São Paulo determinou nesta quinta-feira (8) que o cassino online Stake poderá manter temporariamente sua operação de apostas de quota fixa até 25 de outubro, apesar da Medida Provisória (MP), assinada pelo presidente Lula (PT) , que prevê a extinção das autorizações para funcionamento das plataformas. A decisão é provisória e pode ser revista antes disso.

As bets começaram a deixar de funcionar no Brasil na terça-feira (6) , após a MP do governo federal, anunciada em setembro. A vedação inclui também jogos online e cassinos virtuais no país, como por exemplo, o "Jogo do Tigrinho" (leia mais abaixo).

A juíza Cristiane Farias Rodrigues dos Santos, da 9ª Vara Cível Federal de São Paulo, negou o pedido da empresa para continuar operando até 2029, mas determinou que sua autorização seja preservada temporariamente e que não sejam aplicados bloqueios ou redirecionamentos do site com base apenas na antecipação do fim da autorização.

Ou seja, a decisão não suspende a MP, não declara a medida inconstitucional e não garante o funcionamento da Stake depois de 25 de outubro.

Até lá, a empresa terá de manter mecanismos de identificação e verificação de idade, prevenção à lavagem de dinheiro e proteção ao jogo responsável. Também está proibida de fazer novas campanhas promocionais, bônus para atrair usuários ou ações para ampliar artificialmente sua base (leia mais abaixo).

A decisão também determina a manutenção da possibilidade de saque dos valores disponíveis nas contas dos apostadores.

A Stake havia pedido à Justiça que suspendesse os efeitos da MP em relação à empresa e garantisse sua operação até 31 de dezembro de 2029. Como alternativa, pediu que sua autorização fosse preservada até 25 de outubro.

A juíza considerou que manter a operação por todo o período solicitado significaria, na prática, afastar por longo prazo os efeitos da medida provisória antes que as autoridades apresentassem informações sobre a medida.

Por outro lado, entendeu que o encerramento imediato poderia causar efeitos difíceis de reverter para a empresa, como perda de usuários, contratos, empregos e estruturas de operação . Por isso, decidiu preservar temporariamente a autorização até a data prevista na própria MP.

A Secretaria de Prêmios e Apostas do Ministério da Fazenda, a Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel) e o Banco Central, entre outros órgãos, deverão prestar informações no processo antes de uma nova análise da Justiça.

O g1 procurou o governo federal e a empresa Stake para comentarem a decisão, mas não recebeu retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Veja o que acontece com o dinheiro, as apostas e as contas após o fim das bets. — Foto: g1

De acordo com a autorização provisória, a empresa deverá cumprir algumas regras. Entre elas, manter mecanismos de identificação dos usuários, verificação de idade, prevenção à lavagem de dinheiro, jogo responsável, autoexclusão, pausas e limites de depósito, perda e sessão.

Também estão proibidas, segundo a decisão da Justiça:

apostas por pessoas impedidas por lei ou por programas governamentais;

apostas com recursos provenientes de programas sociais e assistenciais;

iniciativas destinadas a ampliar artificialmente a base de apostadores;

operação por domínios, aplicações, marcas ou estruturas que não estejam abrangidos pela autorização original.

O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) anunciou no dia 25 de setembro, em São Paulo, a proibição total de apostas de quota fixa no país, as chamadas bets. A vedação inclui também jogos online e cassinos virtuais no país, como por exemplo, o "Jogo do Tigrinho".

A proibição, feita a nove dias das eleições, foi formalizada em uma Medida Provisória (MP) assinada pelo presidente Lula. A medida foi publicada em edição extra do Diário Oficial da União (DOU) desta sexta.

🔎As medidas provisórias são editadas pelo governo federal e enviadas ao Congresso Nacional. Para se tornarem leis definitivamente precisam ser votadas em até 120 dias na Câmara dos Deputados e no Senado Federal.

Lula também enviou ao Congresso um projeto de lei que estabelece penas para quem explorar, operar ou divulgar as chamadas bets (veja mais detalhes abaixo).

"Eu tomei a decisão de tomar medida dura e drástica necessária. É como câncer, ou tira tumor, ou tumor vai matar a gente. [...] Foi muita briga, foi muita discussão, foi muito vamos fazer aquilo, faz tudo, faz nada, faz pela metade, não. Já que tem que fazer, vamos fazer o que tem que ser feito. Acabar com as bets", disse Lula.

articles.title: EUA suspendem programa de vistos da Microsoft e outras big techs  | G1
articles.standfirst: Programa suspenso ajuda funcionários estrangeiros da Microsoft e outras big techs a obterem o green card. JD Vance acusou empresas de fraude ao supostamente abusar de vistos temporários, o H1-B, para estrangeiros. Vice-presidente também defendeu investigar universidades.
articles.summary: O governo dos EUA anunciou a suspensão de um programa da Microsoft e de outras big techs para ajudar funcionários estrangeiros a adquirerem o visto permanente nos EUA.
articles.body:
O vice-presidente dos EUA, JD Vance, fala durante entrevista à imprensa sobre iniciativas antifraude do governo norte-americano, em Washington, em 8 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Nathan Howard/ Reuters

O governo de Donald Trump anunciou nesta quinta-feira (8) a suspensão de um programa da Microsoft, da Adobe e de outras big techs para ajudar funcionários estrangeiros a adquirerem o visto permanente nos Estados Unidos, o chamado green card .

O anúncio foi feito pelo vice-presidente dos Estados Unidos, JD Vance. Vance afirmou que o corte é um recado para que a Microsoft contrate mais trabalhadores norte-americanos . Ele acusou ainda a companhia de fraude no programa.

➡️ O programa da Microsoft suspenso pelos EUA é destinado a funcionários da empresa nos Estados Unidos de origem estrangeira . Através dele, a Microsoft ajuda funcionários que chegam aos EUA com um visto temporário a obterem o Green Card.

Além da gigante da tecnologia, o vice disse que a suspensão também será aplicadas a empresas como Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini.

"Não aceitaremos novos pedidos nem processaremos pedidos pendentes de certificação trabalhista permanente que envolvam essas empresas", disse o secretário de Trabalho dos EUA, Keith Sonderling.

Vance acusou a Microsoft de usar o visto H-1B — destinado à contratação temporária de estrangeiros altamente qualificados — de forma abusiva "provavelmente nas últimas décadas" .

"O programa de visto H-1B tem como objetivo permitir que as empresas tragam realmente o melhor dos melhores de fora dos Estados Unidos para posições que são completamente impossíveis de preencher com trabalhadores americanos", disse Vance. "Infelizmente, o programa tem se tornado repleto de fraudes nos últimos anos, provavelmente nas últimas décadas ".

"Se o seu objetivo ao vir para os Estados Unidos da América é receber um cheque do nosso generoso programa de assistência social, então você não vai enriquecer os Estados Unidos da América, e nós preferiríamos que VOCÊ NÃO VIESSE PARA CÁ!", afirmou.

O vice-presidente não explicou, no entanto, com o governo aplicaria a suspensão ao programa da Microsoft, que é privado e interno. A Microsoft ainda não havia se pronunciado até a última atualização desta reportagem.

➡️Embora sua política anti-imigratória foque em imigrantes em situação irregular nos EUA, Donald Trump é um crítico do programa H-1B . Ele argumenta que empresas o utilizam para substituir trabalhadores norte-americanos por mão de obra estrangeira mais barata. Mas diversas empresas afirmam que H-1B supre a escassez de trabalhadores qualificados.

👉 O H-1B é utilizado, principalmente, pelos setores de tecnologia, educação e pesquisa nos EUA. Índia e China são os países das principais nacionalidades contratadas por empresas norte-americanas com esse tipo de visto, segundo a plataforma de dados Visual Capitalist e Statista. O Brasil aparece em 9º lugar da lista .

Detalhe de visto de residência permanente nos EUA. — Foto: Divulgação

Vance também criticou universidades que, segundo ele, estariam abusando do visto J-1 , destinados a estrangeiros que vivem temporariamente nos EUA em programas de intercâmbio de trabalho ou estudo.

O vice-presidente norte-americano defendeu uma investigação a nove universidades, incluindo Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Brown e MIT . Ele disse suspeitar que as instituições também cometam frauderelacionada ao visto J-1 , afirmando que as universidades utilizavam o programa em proporções maiores do que outras instituições semelhantes.

Ele disse ainda que o governo dos EUA vai "reformar" os programas de visto H-1B e J-1 , mas não deu detalhes sobre mudanças.

O anúncio de Vance desta quinta-feira faz parte de uma série de iniciativas do governo Trump para barrar a entrada de estrangeiros nos Estados Unidos por meio de vistos.

Na quarta-feira (7), o governo dos EUA lançou ofensiva contra estudantes internacionais. O Departamento de Segurança Interna propôs uma taxa de US$ 70.000 para estrangeiros que estudem nos EUA e busquem trabalhar nos Estados Unidos .

A regra proposta exigiria que as instituições de ensino pagassem a taxa por cada estudante participante do programa Treinamento Prático Opcional (OPT, na sigla em inglês), que permite aos alunos trabalhar em funções relacionadas à sua área de estudo durante ou após o período acadêmico.

O governo Trump também já limitou a entrada de trabalhadores de países com a China e a Índia nos EUA.

articles.title: Prefeitura de Salvador antecipa feriado escolar do Dia do Professor | G1
articles.standfirst: Mudança vale para as escolas municipais e prolonga a folga após o feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, na segunda-feira (12).
articles.summary: Mudança vale para as escolas municipais e prolonga a folga após o feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, na segunda-feira (12).
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Salvador antecipa feriado escolar do Dia do Professor para 13 de outubro — Foto: Valter Pontes/Secom PMS

A Prefeitura de Salvador antecipou para terça-feira (13) o feriado escolar referente ao Dia do Professor, celebrado em 15 de outubro. A decisão foi publicada na edição de quarta-feira (7) do Diário Oficial do Município (DOM).

Com a mudança, as escolas da rede municipal de ensino não terão aulas no dia 13 de outubro, mas funcionarão normalmente na quinta-feira (15).

A antecipação vai prolongar o período de folga para alunos, professores e outros profissionais da rede municipal, já que a segunda-feira (12) é feriado nacional de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, padroeira do Brasil.

Com isso, quem não tem atividades escolares no fim de semana terá quatro dias consecutivos sem aulas, de sábado (10) até terça-feira (13), com retorno às atividades na quarta-feira (14).

A medida foi oficializada por meio de uma portaria assinada pelo secretário municipal da Educação, Thiago Martins Dantas, e entrou em vigor na data da publicação. A alteração vale apenas para a rede municipal de Salvador.

Procurada pelo g1 , a assessoria de comunicação do Governo da Bahia informou que, na rede estadual de ensino, o feriado escolar segue mantido para 15 de outubro.

Até esta quinta-feira (8), não havia previsão de antecipação da data para os alunos e trabalhadores da rede estadual.

articles.title: VÍDEO mostra confronto de policiais e estudantes em protesto em Paris | G1
articles.standfirst: Adolescentes ficaram gravemente feridos durante a repressão policial aos protestos estudantis na França, que cobram mais investimentos na educação.
articles.summary: Adolescentes ficaram gravemente feridos durante a repressão policial aos protestos estudantis na França, que cobram mais investimentos na educação.
articles.body:
A polícia entrou em confronto com manifestantes em Paris nesta quinta-feira (8), na terceira semana de protestos estudantis que tomaram diversas cidades na França. Os atos têm sido marcados por cenas de violência e repressão policial.

As autoridades têm sido criticadas pela violência aplicada contra os manifestantes - estudantes de ensino médio e de universidades, apoiados por grandes centrais sindicais. A atuação das forças de segurança também é investigada em 18 casos . O governo afirma que a polícia intervém diante de episódios de violência ou danos ao patrimônio.

As passeatas começaram em meados de setembro e ganharam força no fim do mês. As manifestações cobram mais investimentos em educação, contratação de professores substitutos e melhorias na infraestrutura das escolas . Nesta quinta-feira (8), 375 escolas estavam total ou parcialmente fechadas , segundo o ministério da Educação.

Desde o início dos protestos, 6.629 pessoas haviam sido presas, segundo o pasta do Interior. A maioria dos detidos era menor de idade. Também foram registrados confrontos, depredações e incêndios em diferentes pontos do país.

Entre os casos investigados, um estudante de 14 anos teve a mandíbula e vários dentes quebrados após ser atingido no rosto por uma granada de gás lacrimogêneo. Em Lens, um adolescente de 15 anos perdeu uma das mãos em um incidente envolvendo uma granada policial .

Em Tours, um jovem de 16 anos sofreu perda parcial da visão. Após o caso de Lens, o ministro do Interior, Laurent Nuñez, suspendeu temporariamente o uso de um modelo de granada de atordoamento .

Nesta quinta-feira (8), o ministro da Educação Nacional, Édouard Geffray, deve anunciar as primeiras medidas do governo para os estudantes durante o telejornal das 20h da TF1. Os protestos ocorrem na reta final do governo de Emmanuel Macron . A eleição presidencial francesa está prevista para abril de 2027.

Policiais usando equipamento de controle de distúrbios ficam de prontidão diante de manifestantes durante protestos nacionais em Paris, na França. — Foto: Pedro Nunes / Reuters

Os protestos começaram em 17 de setembro e não tem previsão para acabarem — Foto: Reuters

articles.title: Fim do bloqueio: Atendas auxilia empresas a vender e atender  | G1
articles.standfirst: Com API especializado, CRM conversacional e inteligência artificial, plataforma ajuda empresas a estruturar o atendimento, organizar equipes e reduzir riscos operacionais.
articles.summary: Com API especializado, CRM conversacional e inteligência artificial, plataforma ajuda empresas a estruturar o atendimento, organizar equipes e reduzir riscos operacionais.
articles.body:
Atendimento digital: como empresas podem ganhar eficiência e reduzir riscos — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

O WhatsApp se tornou um canal importante para empresas que dependem da comunicação direta com seus clientes. Seja para realizar vendas, esclarecer dúvidas, enviar cobranças ou acompanhar negociações, o aplicativo faz parte da rotina de equipes comerciais e de atendimento.

Mas o que acontece quando um número corporativo é bloqueado no meio do expediente? Para empresas que concentram grande parte de suas operações no WhatsApp, uma interrupção pode comprometer negociações em andamento, atrasar respostas e dificultar o relacionamento com clientes.

É nesse cenário que a Atendas apresenta sua proposta: transformar conversas em uma operação estruturada de relacionamento, com API oficial do WhatsApp, CRM conversacional, automações e recursos de inteligência artificial.

Por que empresas enfrentam bloqueios no WhatsApp Business?

À medida que o volume de conversas aumenta, algumas empresas recorrem a ferramentas de espelhamento ou integrações não oficiais para conectar atendentes e automatizar mensagens. Essas soluções podem trazer riscos operacionais e de conformidade com as políticas do WhatsApp. Práticas de envio inadequadas, como mensagens indesejadas, também podem resultar em restrições.

Quando o canal concentra contatos, históricos e oportunidades comerciais, a interrupção afeta toda a rotina de atendimento. Por isso, além de escolher a tecnologia, é importante adotar processos claros para gerir equipes, bases de contatos e campanhas.

Atendas: WhatsApp oficial integrado à gestão de vendas e atendimento

A Atendas oferece uma plataforma de CRM conversacional que reúne o WhatsApp oficial e recursos de vendas, atendimento e automação. A proposta é permitir que empresas organizem contatos, acompanhem oportunidades comerciais e centralizem conversas em uma operação compartilhada.

A integração por meio da API oficial da Meta reduz a dependência de soluções não autorizadas de espelhamento. Ainda assim, o uso da API não garante imunidade a bloqueios: empresas precisam respeitar as políticas da plataforma e as regras aplicáveis às mensagens enviadas.

Muito além do WhatsApp: conversas que se transformam em oportunidades

A plataforma da Atendas reúne funcionalidades que podem apoiar diferentes etapas do relacionamento com o consumidor:

Atendimento centralizado. Organização das conversas e do histórico de contatos para facilitar o trabalho de equipes.

CRM e gestão comercial. Acompanhamento de oportunidades em funis de vendas e das etapas de negociação.

Inteligência artificial e automação. Recursos para apoiar respostas, qualificação de contatos e encaminhamento a atendentes humanos.

Campanhas e comunicação. Organização de contatos e ações de comunicação, observadas as políticas de cada canal e a legislação aplicável.

Formalização de negócios. Recursos de apoio à jornada comercial, sujeitos à confirmação das funcionalidades contratadas.

Como a centralização ajuda equipes com grande volume de atendimento

Imagine uma empresa com dezenas de vendedores que utilizam o WhatsApp para apresentar propostas e negociar contratos. Sem uma gestão centralizada, uma oportunidade pode ficar sem acompanhamento e informações importantes podem permanecer restritas a um único atendente.

Com um CRM conversacional, a empresa pode organizar interações, distribuir atividades e acompanhar o andamento das negociações. A Atendas apresenta sua solução para operações comerciais e de atendimento que precisam reunir processos, pessoas e canais em uma mesma plataforma.

Case de uso: Parceria entre Atendas e Cartão de Todos recupera R$ 46,7 milhões em oito meses.

A parceria entre a plataforma Atendas e o Cartão de Todos alcançou a marca de R$ 46,7 milhões em valores recuperados entre janeiro e agosto deste ano. Presente em mais de 420 unidades em todo o Brasil, a solução tecnológica otimizou a operação de atendimento e negociação da rede.

Do total recuperado no período, R$ 5,5 milhões (12%) foram transacionados de forma 100% automatizada, sem a necessidade de intervenção humana. A tecnologia também impulsionou novos cadastros, resultando na conversão de mais de 125 mil matrículas por meio de links automáticos.

Outro indicador operacional de destaque foi a taxa Zero de banimento das contas de WhatsApp da operação, garantindo a estabilidade no fluxo de mensagens e o cumprimento das diretrizes da meta do aplicativo.

A API oficial do WhatsApp impede o bloqueio de números?

Não. A API oficial permite que empresas utilizem a infraestrutura destinada à comunicação empresarial, mas não elimina restrições por descumprimento das políticas da Meta. É necessário observar regras de envio, qualidade das interações, permissões aplicáveis e as exigências da Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD).

O uso de uma ferramenta oficial, por si só, não garante conformidade com a LGPD. Cada empresa deve avaliar a base legal para o tratamento de dados, a finalidade das comunicações e os direitos dos titulares.

Para negócios que dependem de conversas digitais para vender e atender, estruturar a operação pode facilitar a organização das equipes e o acompanhamento de oportunidades. Com CRM conversacional, WhatsApp oficial e recursos de automação e inteligência artificial, a Atendas oferece uma plataforma para integrar essas atividades.

articles.title: 'Barriga' a 'chapéu': conheça expressões usadas em redações | G1
articles.standfirst: A partir da própria experiência na redação do GrupoEP, o g1 preparou um glossário com alguns dos principais jargões usados no jornalismo brasileiro.
articles.summary: A partir da própria experiência na redação do GrupoEP, o g1 preparou um glossário com alguns dos principais jargões usados no jornalismo brasileiro.
articles.body:
Quando um jornalista diz que uma reportagem tem um "gancho", que uma pauta virou "suíte" ou que alguém deu uma "barrigada", ele não está falando exatamente o que as palavras costumam significar fora das redações. Esses e outros termos formam um vocabulário próprio usado no dia a dia de uma redação.

➡ A temida "barriga", por exemplo, apesar de parecer uma referência ao corpo humano, é usada nas redações para se referir à publicação de uma informação errada.

A partir da observação da própria rotina na redação do Grupo EP, o g1 Campinas preparou um glossário com alguns dos principais jargões usados no jornalismo brasileiro e que podem ajudar a compreender como funciona a produção de reportagens - confira abaixo.

📰 Esta reportagem faz parte uma série com conteúdos explicativos sobre jornalismo para o "Foca EPronto", concurso de jornalismo universitário promovido pelo GrupoEP em parceria com a PUC-Campinas.

Redação de jornalismo do Grupo EP, em Campinas (SP). — Foto: Isadora de Paiva | Bárbara Camilotti

Barriga ou dar uma barrigada - publicar, de forma não intencional, uma informação incorreta como se fosse verdadeira.

Cabeça - texto lido pelo apresentador antes da exibição de uma reportagem em TV.

Cavar uma pauta - buscar informações, investigar dados ou desenvolver ideias para transformar um assunto em reportagem.

Chapéu - palavra ou expressão curta que aparece acima do título em sites e jornais impressos para introduzir alguma informação sobre a matéria.

Cobertura - acompanhamento jornalístico de um evento ou assunto.

Coletiva - entrevista concedida por uma fonte a diversos veículos simultaneamente.

Deadline - prazo final para entrega ou publicação de um conteúdo. Normalmente é indicado ao pedir posicionamentos ou informações oficiais.

Enxugar o texto - reduzir excessos e tornar a redação mais curta, direta e objetiva.

Escalada - texto falado pelo apresentador na abertura de um telejornal para destacar os principais assuntos que serão abordados ao longo daquela edição

Espelho - planejamento feito pelo editor responsável de um telejornal para organizar por escrito a sequência, o tempo e os temas das reportagens que serão exibidas em cada edição.

Expediente - no jornalismo digital e impresso, espaço onde são informados os responsáveis pela produção de um veículo ou produto jornalístico.

Fact-checking - método de verificação de fatos, dados e declarações.

Factual - notícia motivada por um acontecimento do momento, relacionado a um fato novo.

Foca - termo usado para se referir a jornalistas em início de carreira.

Fonte - pessoa, documento ou instituição que fornece informações.

Furo - notícia divulgada em primeira mão, antes dos veículos concorrentes.

Gaveta - reportagem de caráter atemporal que não precisa ser publicada no mesmo dia em que é produzida.

Lead ou lide - primeiro parágrafo da notícia escrita, responsável por apresentar as informações mais importantes. Costuma responder às perguntas:

Linha fina - texto complementar logo abaixo do título.

Link - participação ao vivo de um repórter durante uma transmissão de televisão

Matéria fria - conteúdo que não depende de um acontecimento imediato e pode ser publicado em diferentes momentos. Semelhante à gaveta.

Matéria quente - reportagem baseada em fatos recentes e com necessidade de publicação rápida.

Nariz de cera - em um texto jornalístico, é uma introdução longa que demora a chegar ao fato principal.

Nota oficial - manifestação formal de uma empresa, órgão público ou instituição sobre determinado tema.

Off - tem dois significados: 1. conteúdo checado com uma fonte que não terá a identidade revelada ou 2. a narração feita pelo repórter que é coberta por imagens em uma reportagem audiovisual.

Outro lado - versão dos fatos apresentada por pessoas ou instituições citadas em uma reportagem de denúncia ou irregularidade. É instrumento obrigatório no jornalismo para assegurar que haja espaço para visões contraditórias em uma reportagem.

Pauta - planejamento da reportagem que prevê o tema, a abordagem, as fontes e o encaminhamento do conteúdo que será produzido.

Personagem - entrevistado cuja história ajuda a ilustrar ou explicar um tema em uma pauta.

Pingue-pongue - entrevista publicada em veículos impressos e online em formato de perguntas e respostas.

Pirâmide invertida - modelo de texto que organiza as informações por ordem decrescente de importância, ou seja, as informações mais importantes constam logo no início do texto e as menos importantes mais para o final.

Povo-fala - formato de entrevista rápida com pessoas abordadas nas ruas sem contato prévio sobre temas gerais.

Quebra-queixo - entrevista coletiva rápida realizada com fontes durante a passagem delas pelo local onde os repórteres de vários veículos estão posicionados em alguma cobertura jornalística de grande repercussão. É geralmente quando o público vê na TV uma aglomeração de jornalistas e vários microfones de emissoras diferentes ao redor de uma mesma pessoa fazendo perguntas.

Release - texto enviado por assessorias de imprensa à imprensa para divulgar um fato relevante ou uma sugestão de pauta sobre seu assessorado.

Ronda - monitoramento ativo e periódico feito por jornalistas da redação junto a fontes, como polícia, bombeiros, Samu, Guardas Municipais, entre outros, para saber se está acontecendo naquele momento do contato algum fato relevante que mereça ser noticiado.

Sonora - material gravado de uma entrevista que será exibida em telejornal.

Suíte - desdobramento ou atualização de uma reportagem já publicada.

Teaser - pequena chamada criada para despertar interesse no público.

Vazamento - divulgação não autorizada de informações sigilosas.

Vender a pauta - convencer editores de que uma ideia merece ser transformada em reportagem.

articles.title: Príncipe Andrew: Justiça anula buscas ilegais ligadas ao caso Epstein | G1
articles.standfirst: As buscas foram 'anuladas' pelo mesmo tribunal em 22 de julho, informou a polícia em um comunicado. A corporação, no entanto, estuda como conservar os materiais apreendidos na operação.
articles.summary: O Príncipe Andrew teve buscas em suas casas anuladas pela justiça britânica após a polícia admitir ilegalidade em operação ligada ao caso Epstein.
articles.body:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor após sair da delegacia de polícia de Aylsham, em Norfolk — Foto: REUTERS/Phil Noble

A polícia britânica reconheceu que as buscas realizadas em fevereiro durante a prisão do ex-príncipe Andrew no âmbito do caso Jeffrey Epstein foram "ilegais", declarou nesta quinta-feira (8) um juiz do Tribunal Superior de Londres.

Essas buscas foram "anuladas" pelo mesmo tribunal em 22 de julho, informou a polícia em um comunicado. A corporação, no entanto, estuda como conservar os materiais apreendidos na operação.

As buscas ocorreram na residência do irmão do rei Charles III em Sandringham, no leste da Inglaterra, e em sua antiga residência em Windsor, cerca de 30 km a oeste de Londres.

Nas primeiras declarações públicas sobre o assunto, o juiz Nicholas Hilliard, do Tribunal Superior de Londres, disse que a polícia havia reconhecido que "os mandados de busca eram ilegais".

No entanto, "isso não encerra a investigação nem significa que toda a investigação tenha sido ilegal", ressaltou o juiz.

Hilliard afirmou que ainda precisa decidir se a polícia pode conservar os bens obtidos mediante um mandado ilegal, como solicitado pela corporação.

Andrew, de 66 anos, foi detido brevemente em 19 de fevereiro por seus vínculos com o falecido criminoso americano Jeffrey Epstein. Ele sempre negou ter cometido qualquer irregularidade relacionada ao caso.

O irmão do rei é investigado por "má conduta no exercício de função pública", sob suspeita de ter transmitido documentos econômicos confidenciais a Epstein quando era enviado especial do Reino Unido para o Comércio, entre 2001 e 2011.

A polícia também informou que examinava uma acusação de agressão sexual apresentada contra ele.

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor ainda não foi formalmente acusado.

Afastado da família real e destituído de seus títulos em 2025, ele foi obrigado a deixar a residência de Royal Lodge, em Windsor, onde vivia havia cerca de 20 anos, para se mudar para a propriedade privada do rei em Sandringham, no condado de Norfolk.

O ex-príncipe foi acusado pela americana Virginia Giuffre de agressões sexuais quando ela tinha 17 anos. Giuffre morreu por suicídio em abril de 2025, aos 41 anos.

articles.title: Forças do Iêmen atropelam combatentes houthis em 'batalha final'  | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo do Iêmen divulgou imagens mostrando veículos de suas forças passando por cima de combatentes rendidos ou caídos. Batalha ocorreu no Estreito de el-Mandeb.
articles.summary: O governo do Iêmen divulgou nesta quinta-feira (8) um vídeo mostrando veículos de suas forças passando por cima de combatentes Houthis nos arredores do Estreito de Bab el-Mandeb.
articles.body:
O governo do Iêmen divulgou nesta quinta-feira (8) um vídeo mostrando veículos de suas forças passando por cima de combatentes Houthis nos arredores do Estreito de Bab el-Mandeb. O atropelamento ocorreu durante uma batalha na qual o governo diz ter reconquistado a área , uma das mais estratégicas do Oriente Médio.

➡️ O estreito, o segundo mais importante do Golfo Pérsico, estava sob controle dos Houthis, apoiados pelo Irã, desde o mês passado. O avanço do grupo terrorista provocou forte impacto no mercado de petróleo e elevou os preços da gasolina e do diesel em todo o mundo.

As imagens divulgadas nesta quinta, verificadas pela agência de notícias Reuters, foram captadas dentro dos veículos blindados do governo. Nelas, é possível ver os veículos atingindo combatentes Houthis. Alguns estavam armados, enquanto outros caminhavam.

No entanto, havia também indivíduos desarmados — alguns sentados, deitados ou agachados na costa arenosa — que não tentaram escapar do veículo que se aproximava e acabaram sendo atropelados.

A Reuters confirmou a localização dos vídeos com base na linha costeira e nas montanhas, elementos que coincidiam com imagens de satélite e com o mapeamento topográfico da região. A data da filmagem foi confirmada pelo governo iemenita, que informou que suas forças haviam retomado a costa ao redor do Estreito de Bab el-Mandeb na segunda-feira (5) .

Estreito de Bab-el-Mandeb, no Mar Vermelho, é a maior rota de exportações de petróleo do Oriente Médio depois do Estreito de Ormuz — Foto: Arte g1

Os homens vistos em solo foram identificados como Houthis, com base em relatos de combates entre os dois grupos na região.

Um comunicado Houthi classificou os vídeos como prova de crimes de guerra , afirmando que eles revelavam "a verdadeira natureza do regime saudita e das forças que ele mobilizou a partir de facções extremistas".

Grupos de defesa dos direitos humanos já acusaram anteriormente os Houthis de crimes de guerra, incluindo ataques de franco-atiradores e disparos de artilharia contra alvos civis, apreensão de ajuda humanitária, maus-tratos a prisioneiros e uso de crianças-soldado. O grupo nega a prática de crimes de guerra.

articles.title: Derry firm becomes one of UK's biggest carpark operators after buying NCP
articles.summary: The Martin Group has become one of the UK's biggest car park operators after buying NCP out of administration.
articles.body:
A Londonderry company has become one of the UK's biggest car park operators after buying NCP out of administration.

The deal means the Martin Group will control more than 100 sites.

The NCP business collapsed in March 2026 after a sustained period of declining performance left it unable to pay its debts.

At that time some of its sites were closed or transferred to other operators.

The administrators, PwC, said the majority of NCP's 145 sites would now transfer to the Martin Group along with the staff who work there.

Zelf Hussain, joint administrator and partner at PwC, said the deal protected hundreds of jobs and delivered the best outcome for creditors.

"Keeping NCP's car parks open also helps keep Britain's town and city centres moving," he added.

"We would like to thank all of NCP's staff and directors for their support and professionalism throughout what has understandably been a period of uncertainty."

NCP's major problems included being locked into long-term leases with property owners and building up a large amount of debt.

The Martin Group already has a substantial commercial property portfolio across the UK including the Fishergate Shopping Centre in Preston and the Mercury Shopping Centre in Romford.

It has recently expanded its hotels business, developing The Bedford Hotel in Belfast and buying The Waterfoot in Derry.

Gary Martin, director of Martin Property Group, said the company's goal was to "build on the strength and heritage of the NCP brand so it can once again deliver the lasting impact on the communities it serves".

"NCP is an iconic brand with a loyal customer base and talented workforce," he added.

Rob England, chief executive of NCP, said it was "a fantastic day for NCP".

"We have had to make difficult, necessary decisions to keep the business moving forward," he said.

England said NCP was "immensely grateful" to its employees, customers and suppliers and its priority was "to restore full operational momentum and build a sustainable platform for long-term growth".

articles.title: Forget dating apps. Young people are cold-calling restaurants to find a date
articles.summary: As young people report burnout from dating apps, they’re looking for the “meet cutes” they heard about from their parents or saw in 2000s rom coms.
articles.body:
"Me and my friends were actually thinking of coming to happy hour in about an hour, and I just wanted to ask if there were, like, any cute guys there?" one girl asks a local restaurant in a video with more than 7.4 million views . "Normalize calling the restaurant to see if there's any cute guys there," she wrote over the video.

Others have called coffee shops and bars asking the same question. "NYC dating is hard ya know," one creator captioned a video calling a West Village restaurant asking if there are any cute guys there. "When Hinge isn't working so you have to call the bars," another creator wrote over a video of her friend calling a bar in Vancouver that racked up 1.5 million views.

While some of the videos are intended for comedic purposes, it's a reflection of the state of dating that young people are increasingly looking to meet offline. As young people report burnout from dating apps, they're increasingly nostalgic for the "meet cutes" they heard about from their parents' generation or watched happen in 2000s rom coms.

"The proliferation of dating apps and now AI-optimizing the dating process has made romance very transactional," Amy Chan , a dating coach and the author of " Unsingle: How to Date Smarter and Create Love that Lasts " previously told USA TODAY. "The 'meet cute' is the antithesis of that. It injects magic and serendipity into the equation."

What's behind the search for a 'meet cute'?

"This is genius," one person commented on a video of women calling a bar. "Honestly I like the idea of getting a bartender to play secret matchmaker for me," wrote another.

It's one of the more creative ways young people are going about searching for in-person opportunities to meet people. There are the influencers who have posted about wearing "I'm Single" hats and "Looking for my future husband" shirts with a QR code. Others have embraced Victorian-era acquaintance cards , viral matchmaking booths and pitch-a-friend style dating events .

There are live comedy dating shows like UpDating and Where There's a Will There's a Way , the dating event series Met Through Friends , which hosts a plus-one party for which each guest must bring a single friend of the opposite sex, and groups like Hot and Social , a company that organizes in-person gatherings for people in their late 20s to 40s to meet.

Eventbrite found a 117% increase in U.S. events using "meet cute" language in the first half of 2026, with attendance up 128% from the same period last year.

There's definitely an interest among young people to get off apps and meet in person. They have app fatigue.

"Constantly swiping and meeting strangers from dating apps are proving to be a recipe for disappointment and dating horror stories," Chan previously told USA TODAY. "Meeting someone in person removes a lot of the barriers that are baked into app dating.

More than half of adults under 30 report having used dating apps like Tinder, Match, Bumble and Hinge, according to 2023 data from Pew Research .

Chan previously told USA TODAY that the "short-form, swipe-heavy nature of modern dating culture" complicates dating. She said the paradox of choice on apps fosters a "shopping cart mentality" where daters evaluate users as if they were products.

That algorithmic loop can be exhausting, and a Forbes Health survey found that 79% of Gen Zers report burnout from apps.

With horror stories and red flags amplified on social media, Chan told USA TODAY that trust levels are also lower than ever.

And apps are responding — Tinder in March launched an events tab in select markets. In NYC, 66% of Gen Z users have engaged with the feature, according to Global Chief Marketing Officer Melissa Hobley. A wave of new apps like Cerca and Frnds of Frnds have popped up with the premise of connecting users through mutual friends.

"For most of human history, you met people through friends, community, work, school, and there were social consequences if you behaved poorly," Chan said. "The apps removed that, and now it seems like the market demand is putting it back in."

What modern dating trends say about Gen Z

Gen Z's dating style reflects a deeper trend of risk aversion — young people are also drinking less and having less sex . While those things can be positive, they're also indicators that some Gen Zers are socially isolated. Much of Gen Z missed out on pivotal years in the classroom or office during the pandemic, impacting their ability to socialize.

"If you're not really forced to be in these social situations and lack the social skills, the path of least resistance is to avoid," Chan said. "It's easy to stay home, play video games, watch porn, even get an AI girlfriend to give temporary hits of dopamine and a false sense of intimacy."

A nationwide reckoning with the #MeToo Movement, evolving gender roles in the home and workplace, the rise of viral, online cancel culture and steep political polarization have reshaped the social norms around how men and women engage. Young people are less likely to approach others in person romantically, according to Chan, primarily due to fear of rejection or being perceived as intrusive.

All of these elements have made the "meet cute" appealing. Chan called it the "analog version of romance."

"This generation never got to experience dating before app culture, doom scrolling and social media," Chan told USA TODAY. "They're not longing for something they lost, they're longing for an idea of something — something that must have been better than what their current reality is."

articles.title: Transgender woman deported to Central African Republic in hiding and worried
articles.summary: Daniela Fuentes said she does not understand why she was sent to Africa rather than her home country of Cuba.
articles.body: DAKAR, Senegal — In Miami, Daniela Fuentes styled hair for clients and performed in drag at a nightclub called Azúcar. She wore her blond wig in public and dressed as the woman she had known herself to be since adolescence in Cuba. Now, more than 6,000 miles (10,000 kilometers) away in the Central African Republic, she wears men’s clothes, lowers her voice and tries not to draw attention to the breasts she developed after beginning hormone treatment as a teenager. As part of U.S. efforts to deport people to countries other than their own, authorities sent her Aug. 29 to a place where she has no ties and where advocacy groups have reported arbitrary detention, torture, and other rights violations of sexual and gender minorities. “Everything is difficult here because I have to hide who I am,” said Fuentes, a 32-year-old transgender woman living on a compound she rarely leaves, sharing a room with four Cuban men also deported from the U.S. “I don’t know this place, the people or the language, and I have no idea what will happen to me.” The Central African Republic — one of the world’s poorest countries, a place with a history of conflict that the U.S. State Department advises American travelers to avoid — is one of at least 12 African nations that signed agreements to accept “third-country” deportations, a policy the U.S. Supreme Court last month allowed to continue, at least temporarily. In the Central African Republic — where transgender people have little to no legal protections and are marginalized in much of society — Fuentes dons her wig only in the privacy of her bathroom. She described disguising herself as protection, first in U.S. detention and now in a country she first heard of when she was already headed there on a deportation flight. “My whole life, my whole identity, was taken away from me,” Fuentes said. Public records say a judge ordered Fuentes to leave the U.S. but offer no other information. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials did not reply to emailed questions. Tens of thousands of people have been deported to ‘third countries’ Fuentes’ compound in the capital, Bangui, is an apartment complex where the government houses male deportees. Fuentes said she can leave but that officials have advised her and others to avoid it — they have no identification, which could lead to issues with the police. It also means they can’t work, she said, and she’s waiting on travel documents that would allow her to leave the country. The International Organization for Migration, an agency associated with the United Nations, has provided food, and the migrants say they’ve crowdsourced for donations to buy groceries. The U.S. — via agreements often not made public — has deported about 25,000 people to more than two dozen countries that aren’t their own, the vast majority to Mexico, according to a tally by Third Country Deportation Watch, a partnership of Refugees International and Human Rights First. The U.S. has not released numbers or details. From January 2025 to August 2026, more than 500 were sent to countries in Africa, according to a Human Rights Watch report published Thursday — including at least 12 people who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual or transgender and were deported to places that criminalize same-sex relations or public same-sex romantic conduct. Some advocates say the number is likely higher. “These are not bureaucratic errors or isolated incidents,” said Bridget Crawford, of the group Immigration Equality. “They are the predictable result of policies that purposefully abandon our legal and moral obligation to protect LGBTQ+ immigrants fleeing persecution.” The U.S. government says the policy is lawful and that receiving governments provide assurances deportees won’t be persecuted or tortured. Fuentes grew up in La Lisa, on Havana’s outskirts, and said she understood from childhood that she was different. She began living as a woman in adolescence and started taking hormones at 18. She ran a salon from her home, coloring and cutting hair. She said she was harassed because of her gender identity and attacked at least twice, leaving scars on her arm and head. Police also questioned her about operating a private business, she said — though housefront businesses are common in the area. In 2023, Fuentes sold her home and left amid a deepening economic crisis and a crackdown on dissent — even as Cuba, one of Latin America’s most progressive countries for LGBTQ+ rights, adopted new inclusion laws. Making her way to the U.S., she said, she presented as a man traveling through Central America; she believed it was safer. After seven months in Mexico, she said, she entered the U.S. through Texas via CBP One, a President Joe Biden-era online appointment system that allowed migrants to live in the country for two years on humanitarian grounds. Then she went to Miami. There, she began living openly as a woman again. She found work styling hair and performed at Azúcar. Though she lacked permanent legal status, Fuentes said Miami offered something she’d rarely experienced: the freedom to move through daily life as herself. That ended when officers encountered her outside a motel. Fuentes said they learned she had missed an immigration court hearing in Texas. She said she asked that the case be moved to Florida but received no response. Fuentes said she was taken into custody and later placed in immigration detention with men. Officials confiscated her wig and gave her a male detainee’s uniform, she said. Such treatment is in line with a January 2025 executive order directing officials to exclude transgender women from women’s prisons and detention centers. “When I learned that they were going to put me with men, I almost fainted,” Fuentes said. Deportees said they boarded a flight without knowing the destination Fuentes was held at two detention facilities in Florida, then transferred to Texas. When armed officers arrived there, she said, she suspected she was facing deportation, but they didn’t reveal she was being sent to Africa until about five hours into the flight. Other deportees on the flight told AP they also weren’t told the destination until they were on the plane. Dozens have been sent to the Central African Republic, including an Iranian woman facing persecution in her home country and an Afghan whose brothers worked with the U.S. military. Fuentes said she does not understand why she was sent to Africa rather than Cuba. She told AP she has no lawyer. The U.S. does repatriate Cuban citizens, as part of agreements to resume deportation flights in 2023, despite tensions in relations between the countries. Charter flights have arrived in Havana regularly. Yasmany Moreno, another Cuban deportee in Bangui, said that upon arriving, the group had no visas or documents establishing their legal status in the country. Officials spoke of providing assistance for 90 days, he said, but the deportees didn’t know what would happen afterward or where they would live. Several told AP their longer-term status remained unclear and that U.S. authorities had taken their identity documents. A policy officer at the Central African Republic’s Foreign Ministry said the deportees are in “good hands” and are being monitored by the International Organization for Migration. He spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to discuss the matter publicly. The U.S. this year committed to $85 million in funding to IOM for Central African Republic operations including “assistance to migrants” and “community stabilization.” IOM says migrants can seek asylum in the country, request assistance to return home or get help traveling to another place they’re authorized to enter. It referred questions about the deportees’ status and individual cases such as Fuentes’ to Central African Republic officials. A government spokesperson didn’t reply to phone calls and text messages seeking comment. Human Rights Watch’s report says some people deported to third countries face detention, abuse and the prospect of persecution. Eswatini has held deportees in a maximum-security prison without charges. Equatorial Guinea has held them against their will at a hotel owned by the president’s family. “Several of these African governments are not only complicit in U.S. abuses but have violated the human rights of these deported people themselves,” Michael Garcia Bochenek, of Human Rights Watch, said in a statement. Fuentes and other deportees say they can’t work, with most days spent at the compound Fuentes said the Cuban men in her room know she is a woman and look out for her. She rarely feels safe enough to leave. Once, at a supermarket, workers pointed at her breasts and initially refused to sell her fruit, she said. Other people in Bangui have mocked her and pointed at her. “My personal appearance is awful,” she said. “I look like a different human being.” Moreno described restrictions on the group’s movements, saying officers accompanied them to the market and on occasional outings but restricted them from going out at night. Fuentes and Moreno said they have no passports or other identification and cannot work. Most days, Fuentes remains at the compound, looking at her phone and waiting for travel documents. She said Cuba has agreed to accept her return — a Cuban embassy document shows she is authorized. But Fuentes said she hopes to seek asylum elsewhere, possibly Canada. “The harassment and economic hardship that caused me to flee still remain,” she said.

articles.title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed', court hears
articles.summary: The girl told police there was "blood all over my hands" following the attack, a court hears.
articles.body:
A schoolgirl who was stabbed by a masked fellow pupil at school described how she told a teacher "Sir, I've been stabbed" after the attack.

Police were called to Thorpe St Andrew School, near Norwich, on 11 March, following reports that a 15-year-old girl had been stabbed in the back.

The defendant, who is now 16 and cannot be named for legal reasons, has denied a charge of attempted murder, but has admitted possessing a kitchen knife without lawful authority and wounding with intent.

In a police interview played to the jury at King's Lynn Crown Court, the girl said she had been in "panic mode" and felt numb and weak.

Describing the attack, which took place in a corridor, she said she had seen a masked person dressed "head to toe in black, no school uniform whatsoever".

The boy did not say anything to her and she did not recognise him, she added.

She said she turned away and it "felt like he touched me on the shoulder, then it felt like he punched me".

She said she "didn't know I was stabbed at this point" but after turning into a classroom, "I went 'Sir, I've been stabbed.'"

The girl said the school lockdown bell sounded and staff gave first aid.

Of the incident itself, she said that once she had opened the door, "I felt sharp pain shooting through my back, I went like that and it was blood all over my hands".

She said in the interview, carried out days after the incident: "I don't think it's hit me properly yet.

Stephen Rose KC, for the defence, asked the girl, who gave evidence in court, whether she had had any issues with the boy. She said she had not.

She wiped tears from her eyes and asked for a break during her evidence.

Another female pupil at the school, who witnessed the attack, said in a video-recorded police interview that the boy "came up behind [the girl] and just stabbed her in the back near her shoulder".

She said she "didn't think he realised I was there until after he did it" and that she ran off and told a teacher.

Asked at what point she had first seen the knife, she said: "As he raised it."

The court has already been told that the defendant had written notes saying he hated women .

One note, which prosecutors said was found by police pinned to the wall of his bedroom, said: "My barren world... Hello. To all readers out there in the UK and perhaps even the world. If you're reading this, I am either dead or in custody.

"I imagine the police will be the first to read this and seize it as evidence, so I will make something very clear. I made this decision to do so on my own."

Another note read: "Am I evil for that? Probably. Am I an incel? A misogynist? No. I just have good judgement."

Christopher Paxton KC, in opening the prosecution case, said: "We, the prosecution, say his intention is made plain not just by those moments of the stabbing, but made plain by his notes and his obsession with killing and being fuelled by hatred."

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepts three Houthi ballistic missiles
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia says two of the missiles intercepted were headed towards the capital, Riyadh.
articles.body:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting on behalf of Yemen’s internationally recognised government says it has intercepted ballistic missiles allegedly fired by Yemen’s Houthis towards cities in Saudi Arabia.

In a statement, coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said his forces intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles heading in the direction of the Saudi capital Riyadh, and one missile in the direction of the city of Khamis Mushait, close to the Yemeni border, on Thursday.

Separately, Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency said in a statement on X that falling debris from an intercepted missile had caused material damage to a kindergarten and medical clinic complex in Riyadh. It did not indicate if there were any casualties.

Yahya Saree, Yemen’s Houthi military spokesman, said the Iran-aligned group launched a ballistic missile towards King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday afternoon, claiming that the missile had successfully hit its intended target, causing damage and disrupting air traffic.

Witnesses told The Associated Press news agency that they heard several explosions in Riyadh on Thursday, including one at the city’s airport that halted flights. Al Jazeera could not independently confirm the reports.

In recent days, the Houthis have warned aviation companies to avoid using Saudi airspace, saying any aircraft operating in the kingdom’s airspace, except over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, is a target for the Houthis.

Following the latest reports, Air India said on Thursday that it had cancelled flights to and from Riyadh until at least the weekend, and the Germany-based Lufthansa ⁠Group ⁠airlines said they were suspending flights to Riyadh through October 16, according to the Reuters news agency.

The US embassy in Saudi Arabia meanwhile urged its citizens in the country to remain vigilant, saying they should be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions.

Saudi Arabia’s Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh were targeted in two separate attacks, claimed by the Houthis on Tuesday and Wednesday. At least three civilians were killed and 36 injured, according to a statement from the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA).

Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the attacks on the two airports, saying in a post on X that they “represent a grave violation of the Kingdom’s sovereignty and a direct threat to the security of the region and the safety of civilians, civil objects, and air navigation”. Oman and Egypt also condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi airports.

These were not the first Houthi strikes on Saudi airports. On September 18, Saudi-led coalition forces said they intercepted and destroyed a suspected Houthi ballistic missile fired towards the airport in Riyadh from Yemen.

A day later, on September 19, at least one explosion was heard near the airport in Riyadh, and a large plume of black smoke was seen rising from a fuel storage area at King Khalid International Airport.

Meanwhile, inside Yemen, explosions have been reported near the airport in the Houthi-controlled Red Sea port city of Hodeidah, according to local sources.

The cause and impact of these explosions are not immediately clear.

In a post on X, a spokesman for Yemen’s Saudi-backed forces said at least 1,370 Houthi fighters were “neutralised” in 1,729 operations, and at least 300 vehicles were destroyed or disabled.

Al Jazeera’s Hadeel al-Yamani, reporting from Taiz in Yemen, said intense fighting is raging between armed forces of Yemen’s internationally recognised government and the Houthis in al-Shamayatayn, al-Maafer and the southern and western countryside of Taiz governorate.

“The Houthis are pushing into rural areas that have not seen conflict for years, aiming to open a supply route because their lines towards al-Kadaha and al-Waziiya, which link Aden, Lahij and Taiz, are nearly cut off by advancing government forces”, she said.

Al-Yamani added that pro-government forces are within striking distance of al-Waziiya and the Kahboub Mountains overlooking Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

Pro-government forces have reported more than 2,000 operations against the Houthis, and are preparing for a “dangerous escalation”, she said.

More than 200,000 people have been displaced from their homes since fighting in Yemen escalated in recent weeks, according to data released by the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

The IOM described the crisis in a statement on Wednesday as alarming, with the number of people displaced surging from the 76,000 recorded in mid-September.

articles.title: RAF Molesworth: Men arrested on suspicion of trespass at US base
articles.summary: Police say they apprehended two Latvian men at about 02:00 BST while they were inside the perimeter.
articles.body:
Two Latvian men were arrested after a fence was breached at an RAF base used by the US military and Nato for intelligence operations, counter-terrorism police have said.

The alert was raised when a Ministry of Defence Police (MDP) security patrol at RAF Molesworth identified an abandoned vehicle at about 22:00 BST on Wednesday.

Searches revealed a small breach of the fence at the site in Cambridgeshire, and a few hours later, police said the pair were arrested inside the perimeter.

The two men are aged 36 and 32 and live in the UK, the Met Police said.

The force's Counter Terrorism Policing London is investigating and commander Helen Flanagan said officers were not currently linking it to the high-profile incident in Gloucestershire.

"We're very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites, but at this stage there is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford last week," said Flanagan.

However, she stressed the inquiry was in its "very early stages".

They were initially arrested on suspicion of trespass on a prohibited site and criminal damage - after Cambridgeshire Police officers joined the search - and were taken to a local station.

The pair were later arrested on suspicion of an offence under Section 4 of the National Security Act 2023 – namely entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK.

RAF Molesworth is home to the US's intelligence operations centres for Europe and Africa, as well as a Nato intelligence hub.

Flanagan also said police were carrying out two searches at addresses in the Peterborough area.

"A big part of this is looking at any potential motivation as to why the men were present at the site, but I must stress we are keeping an open mind at this stage," she said.

"As ever, I would ask the public to remain vigilant and if you see anything of concern, then to contact police."

The A1M was partially closed at about 13:00 BST earlier, along with several other roads in the Glatton area, because of the abandoned vehicle.

A cordon was put in place while it was examined by bomb squad officers but the roads were reopened shortly after as Cambridgeshire Police said "nothing of concern was identified".

RAF Molesworth is located west of Huntingdon, close to the border with Northamptonshire.

A Ministry of Defence spokesperson said: "We remain highly vigilant to potential threats against defence sites and work closely with the police and our allies to keep them secure.

"The protection of our bases is kept under constant review, with a multi-layered approach that includes physical barriers, patrols, surveillance, monitoring, and counter-drone capabilities."

A spokesperson for US European Command thanked UK agencies for their support, but added: "It is inappropriate to discuss matters of intelligence, and we will not discuss specific force protection measures.

"We will continue to assess the threat environment surrounding our installations and take appropriate actions to protect our people, our platforms, and the bases where our forces operate from."

articles.title: Birmingham Airport unveils £2bn plan for 30 million passengers
articles.summary: The first stage of development, upgrading baggage systems and terminals, could start in 2027.
articles.body:
Birmingham Airport has announced a £2bn expansion plan which bosses say could more than double passenger numbers and create thousands of jobs.

The draft plan, a spokesperson said, sets out the use of existing runway capacity alongside "significantly enhanced" passenger facilities over the next 15 years.

Unveiling an eight-week public consultation, chief executive Nick Barton said the scheme aims to ensure the airport was "ready for the future" but needed a "fair and stable taxation environment".

Transport secretary Heidi Alexander said the government was "backing our aviation sector to continue growing, right across the country".

In 2025, the airport said it had seen a record year with more than 13 million passengers travelling through it. Bosses want to see this rise by more than double, up to 30 million a year.

Airport chiefs said the proposals set out a "clear commitment" to continue serving the region and create more than 50,000 jobs, including 3,800 at the airport site.

They added that they wanted to make sure the growth was "delivered responsibly and sustainably" for the people living closes to the site.

The first stage of development could start in 2027, with significant investments in areas such as baggage and terminal facilities, additional aircraft stands and improvements in surface access.

Hundreds of passengers were affected by issues with the airport's baggage system in August , with many left without their luggage.

People can give feedback on the plans online, by post or attend any of the 20 events, which start in Hampton on Arden on 16 October .

"The £2bn proposed investment is unprecedented at Birmingham Airport and will take our airport close to 30 million passengers," said Barton.

"This level of ambition sends a strong signal of support and confidence in our airport and wider region.

However, Barton added that the plan came at a time the airport was faced with increased running costs from wage bills, energy prices and taxation.

"Unless tax and regulatory environments are made more favourable and stable for major infrastructure investment, they [the plans] may not materialise," he said.

Alexander said the city's plan was a "massive boost" to the West Midlands, unlocking investment and "creating 50,000 well-paid local jobs to get people into employment".

Richard Parker, the Labour mayor of the West Midlands, also welcomed the "ambitious masterplan" which he said would improve international links and unlock vital backing for local businesses and supply chains.

"This consultation gives local people and business owners a chance to have their say and help shape the airport's expansion so that it brings lasting benefits for our communities," he said.

articles.title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
articles.summary: The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.
articles.body:
Prosecutors in the United States have accused Venezuela's former leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, of conspiracy to commit torture.

The fresh charges against the couple were made public on Thursday and are in addition to the drug-trafficking and weapons charges already brought against them, which they have denied.

Maduro, 63, and Flores, 69, have been in custody since January in a detention centre in Brooklyn, where they were taken after US forces seized them in a pre-dawn raid on their compound in the Venezuelan capital, Caracas.

Barry J Pollack, Maduro's attorney, said his client denies the new charges and looks forward to his day in court.

Federal prosecutors also announced on Thursday that Flores was added to the earlier narco-terrorism charge.

The trial for both Maduro and Flores is set to begin in June 2027.

Both are being held in a detention centre in Brooklyn and are expected to remain there after Flores's request to be moved to house arrest was denied by a judge on Thursday.

The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens who were being held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.

The superseding indictment unsealed on Thursday accuses the former presidential couple of "entrenching themselves in power" by presiding "over a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention, and the torture of detainees, including United States citizens".

According to the indictment, the torture included "electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture".

The prosecutors allege that the psychological torture included threats to kill victims' families, including children.

"All of this was done to ensure that Maduro and Flores retained their power," prosecutors said outside the courthouse on Thursday.

"This conduct, we allege, has caused significant harm to Americans, to US citizens", prosecutors said, calling it "the epitome of corruption".

The prosecution accuses Flores of having played a key role in the development of the repressive system, ordering that individuals be tortured and even receiving updates on the torture of specific prisoners.

The court document alleges that she did so in order to protect members of her family who were involved in illegal activities.

The allegations contained in the superseding indictment echo many of the accusations long made by prisoners who have been released from detention in Venezuela.

Javier Tarazona, the head of a human rights group in Venezuela, told BBC Mundo's Norberto Paredes earlier this year how he and his brother were held in a tiny punishment cell for 46 days after being arbitrarily arrested.

Another former inmate, Ángel Godoy, told BBC Mundo that he was kept isolated for months and not allowed to contact his wife, who was in turn kept in the dark about his whereabouts.

The allegations listed in the superseding indictment made public on Thursday relate to cases during Maduro's time in power.

After his ouster, his vice-president, Delcy Rodríguez, was sworn in as interim leader with the backing of the Trump administration.

While hundreds of political prisoners have been released under an amnesty law since she has taken over power, more than 300 still remain behind bars, according to prisoners' rights group Foro Penal.

The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk has warned that his office has received reports alleging that detainees continue to be tortured even after the seizure of Maduro.

Türk said in March that "structural and systemic human rights concerns" had persisted in Venezuela despite Maduro's ousting.

Venezuela's foreign minister at the time accused Türk of parroting the agenda of "extremists" by citing the allegations.

articles.title: Venezuela’s Nicolas Maduro and his wife charged over torture allegations
articles.summary: The new US charge adds to the existing drug trafficking case against Venezuela’s former president and first lady.
articles.body:
Former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, were charged in the US state of New York with conspiring to commit torture in connection with allegations that they tortured political opponents to maintain their power.

The indictment, filed on Thursday in a Manhattan federal court, adds one count of conspiracy to commit torture to the drug trafficking charges the couple already faced.

It alleges that Maduro and Flores were part of a conspiracy that used torture and other abuses to repress and punish political opponents. Prosecutors say the conspiracy ran from at least 1999 through 2025 and involved Venezuelan military, intelligence and law enforcement officials.

The indictment details several cases of alleged torture. One detainee was allegedly subjected to electric shocks and asphyxiation after being arrested following a 2018 drone attack that the Venezuelan government said was an attempt to assassinate Maduro.

The alleged abuses also extended to United States citizens detained in Venezuela, three of whom were cited in the indictment. In one case, in January 2025, Venezuelan intelligence officers arrested an American citizen who was not their intended target and beat him repeatedly over two days, which caused permanent injury to his eye. He was reportedly released about a year later and was warned by Venezuelan officials not to disclose that the government had abused him.

Prosecutors allege that Maduro personally directed or was regularly briefed on the abuse of detainees. In one instance, the indictment says Maduro was told that a detained military officer remained defiant and responded by ordering officials to “squeeze them harder”. Prosecutors say he went so far as to suggest specific torture methods for unrelenting victims.

In other cases, prosecutors allege Maduro was told about beatings, electric shocks and simulated drowning and directed officials to apply additional “pressure”. According to the indictment, Flores was present at some of the meetings where detainees and their treatment were discussed.

“The indictment … alleges conduct that is truly unthinkable. The members of Maduro’s broad conspiracy were not just sitting behind a desk,” said federal prosecutor Jamie McDonald at a news conference. “These members of the conspiracy were holding the shovel. American citizens were tortured, and so were thousands of Venezuelans, we allege.”

Maduro and Flores pleaded not guilty to the drug charges and have been held at Brooklyn’s Metropolitan Detention Center since their capture. Their trial is scheduled for June 1, 2027.

The charges pile on an ongoing criminal case against Maduro and Flores. A superseding indictment accuses Maduro of working with cartel groups to move cocaine through Venezuela towards the US.

Maduro was abducted and imprisoned on January 3, after US President Donald Trump authorised a military raid in Caracas.
