articles.title: Christa Pike wasn't alone in her crime. What happened to accomplices
articles.summary: Two other people were involved in the crime that landed Christa Pike on death row. Here's what happened to them, and why they got lesser punishments.
articles.body:
While Christa Pike didn't act alone in the crime that landed her on death row , the two others involved in the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer met less severe punishments.

Pike, Tadaryl Shipp and Shadolla Peterson were all students at Jobs Corps, a training program in Knoxville, Tennessee, when they lured Slemmer, a classmate, into the woods on Jan. 12, 1995.

There, Pike and Shipp, a couple at the time, tortured Slemmer and bludgeoned her to death. They were both later convicted of the crime, while Peterson pled guilty and walked away with probation, according to court records.

The grisly crime has garnered renewed interest after Pike's botched execution by lethal injection on Sept. 30. She was transported to a hospital and has since regained consciousness and is speaking , her attorney said on Oct. 7.

Here's what to know about the other assailants in the case that's capturing national attention.

Protests and emotional reactions as Tennessee botches Christa Pike execution

Christa Pike accomplice Tadaryl Shipp serving life sentence

Shipp was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit first-degree murder at a 1997 trial. He was sentenced to life and 25 years in prison, according to court and inmate records.

Because Shipp was 17 at the time of the crime, he could not get the death penalty under state law.

After Slemmer's murder, Shipp told police he "had dabbled in satanism since he was 10 years old," according to a 1998 appellate ruling.

When he and Pike were taken into custody two days after the murder, they were both wearing pentagram necklaces, and Shipp told police he had "satanic paraphernalia" in his room at the Job Corps campus.

Shipp told police he carved a pentagram into Slemmer's chest because he thought she could be "a satanic sacrifice."

According to WATE and WBIR , Shipp was denied parole in October 2025. The 48-year-old will be eligible for parole again in 2031.

Other accomplice, Shadolla Peterson, got probation

Peterson, the other individual involved in the crime, pleaded guilty to being an accessory and received a sentence of six years probation, per court documents.

She took a plea deal from prosecutors and received credit for 460 days in jail, according to a 1996 article in the Knoxville News Sentinel, part of the USA TODAY Network.

While Peterson had initially been indicted on a murder charge, prosecutors said if the case had gone to trial, they would only have proof that she was present at the murder, not that she was involved in the killing, according to the article.

The public defender who represented Peterson told the outlet at the time that she admitted to being present at the killing but denied taking part in the attack and did not know Slemmer was going to be murdered.

On Jan. 12, 1995, Pike asked Slemmer to accompany her to a Blockbuster store before luring her into the woods, she told police.

Pike – who had brought a box cutter and meat cleaver with her – and Shipp attacked Slemmer, bludgeoning her and eventually cutting her stomach and throat with the box cutter, according to court documents .

During the attack, as Slemmer bargained for her life, Pike "told Slemmer to 'shut up' because it 'was harderto hurt somebody when they're talking to you,'" she later told police, per court documents.

Shipp also carved a pentagram into Slemmer's chest, and Pike – who told police she believed Slemmer was interested in her boyfriend – later showed off a piece of Slemmer's skull to a friend.

Slemmer's body was found on Jan. 13, 1995. A Tennessee Grounds Department employee first mistook her body for the corpse of an animal because of how badly she had been beaten, according to court records .

Born on Sept. 20, 1975, Slemmer was raised in Orange Park, Florida, but moved to Knoxville to enroll in Jobs Corps, according to court records and the Nashville Tennessean, part of the USA TODAY Network .

May Martinez, Slemmer's mother, told WBIR-TV that her daughter loved roller skating, computers and playing old games with her family.

"She was a nerd," Martinez told the station. "But a good nerd."

Christa Pike latest: Attorney says she is 'angry' after botched execution

Officials in Tennessee attempted to execute Pike on Sept. 30, but she survived two doses of pentobarbital injections and was taken to a Nashville-area hospital.

Pike's attorney Randy Spivey said she woke up and began speaking on Oct. 7. He believes the first words she said were, "where am I and who are you?"

"She is angry and confused about everything right now," Spivey said, adding that she is "very aware the state tried to execute her."

Pike has a blood clot in one of her arms, pneumonia and swelling in her hands and arms, Spivey said. She is unable to swallow or move her arms and it's unclear what kind of function she will regain.

Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee has ordered an investigation into what went wrong and called off the state's only remaining lethal injection this year. Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada also announced his resignation after the incident.

articles.title: Bronx man who allegedly threw a woman and her baby off a 15th-floor balcony is arrested
articles.summary: A 31-year-old man has been arrested in New York City following a manhunt for the person allegedly responsible for pushing a woman to her death from a 15th-floor balcony as she was holding her 8-month-old daughter.
articles.body: A 31-year-old man has been arrested in New York City following a manhunt for the person allegedly responsible for pushing a woman to her death from a 15th-floor balcony as she was holding her 8-month-old daughter. The New York City Police Department tracked down Angel Carrasco late Wednesday, hours after identifying him as the prime suspect in Nathaly Ramirez’s death. Investigators said the 23-year-old mother was holding her daughter when she was shoved from the balcony on Olinville Avenue, in the Allerton section of the Bronx, early Tuesday. Both plunged to the ground. Ramirez was pronounced dead at a hospital. The baby girl was taken there as well and remained in critical condition as of Wednesday. Authorities believe her mother’s body may have cushioned her fall. Officials said Carrasco was hiding out at a friend’s house when police caught up to him. He faces charges of murder, attempted murder, manslaughter, attempted manslaughter and assault. Police were reviewing surveillance video as part of their investigation. The video shows a man walking away in a hooded sweatshirt as police responded to the scene, police sources said. Sources said there was a history of domestic violence at Ramirez’s address, and police were looking to question her ex-boyfriend after the deadly incident. A witness who lives in the Allerville Arms apartment building said she heard yelling in the middle of the night before screams led people to find Ramirez’s body outside. A neighbor told NBC New York she heard the young woman pleading with someone before she and her baby plunged from the balcony. “I heard her yelling and screaming, ‘Please don’t do this. My baby. You know my baby is scared. Look at her face,’” the neighbor said. “Next thing you know, I hear her scream, and I see something hit the ground.” A high school classmate from the Bronx Leadership Academy who stopped by the growing memorial said he’d remember the young mother as a kind person. “She was always cool with everybody. She always talked to everybody,” he said. If she saw someone having a bad day, he said Ramirez would “joke with them to life their day up.” CORRECTION: (Oct. 8, 2026, 12:45 p.m. ET): A photo caption in a previous version of this article misstated the number of fatalities. This story has been updated to reflect that the baby girl remained in critical condition as of Wednesday.

"She is up and walking for the first time today, but just around the room, not very far." articles.title: Curo service charge legal battle win for Weston residents
articles.summary: People living in a block of flats take their landlord to tribunal over a 300 per cent increase.
articles.body:
Residents living in a block of flats have won a legal battle against their housing association - after being faced with a service charge increase of more than 300 per cent.

Nine families living in Weston-super-Mare in Somerset had seen their monthly fees go up from about £70 per month to more than £300 a month.

Housing provider Curo has now agreed to limit the charge to just over £100 after being taken to tribunal.

A spokesperson for Curo said that it had "already agreed these reductions before the tribunal took place".

Curo continued: "What we're trying to avoid is large bills that leaseholders aren't expecting.

"Keeping people safe is our priority, and we need to balance ensuring the right fire safety measures are in place with trying to minimize the financial impact, which we know has been difficult."

Alan Rice from Weston Housing Action said the residents are "ecstatic".

"Quite a few people told us that we wouldn't win, but we were persistent and we got the result we wanted", he added.

Multi-million pound revamp of Clifton Suspension Bridge complete

The dispute related to a property called Coombe Lodge.

It contains nine flats, all of which are shared ownership - a scheme designed to help people get onto the housing ladder by buying a portion of their property, and paying rent to a landlord for the remainder.

When the service charge went up, one resident said they had to take on an extra job, while others said they were anxious they'd be unable to afford the higher fee.

Curo said the extra money was primarily to increase the block's sinking fund, which acts as a long-term savings account for building costs.

Rice said that while there is "some need" for a sinking fund, it was "devastating" for residents.

He said: "Although they were sold to them as affordable homes, suddenly they weren't affordable any more."

The residents will now be reimbursed the excess charges they have paid.

In response, Curo said "There are always maintenance costs linked to owning a flat in a block, and we completely understand that these can be a shock when significant work is needed.

"That's why there are sinking funds, which are like a 'savings account' for the whole building, to help flat owners spread the cost across several years."

The provider said it hoped it can "continue to work constructively with residents at Coombe Lodge to resolve all the remaining issues going forward".

There is no limit on how much a service charge can increase, but a law passed in 2024 should eventually force managing agents to provide a full breakdown of costs.

The Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act is yet to be fully implemented. It promises leaseholders clearer service charge bills, and the right to look back at service charge information over the past six years

Samantha Young lives in a Curo-managed block in Twerton in Bath, and said she is going to take her case to the ombudsman after her annual service charge rose from £990 to more than £6,000, which she described as "astronomical."

"It is absolutely not affordable. This is higher than what you'd paid in zone one in London for flats with gyms and concierges.

"It quite frankly feels like we're receiving nothing."

Curo told the BBC it was "having ongoing conversations with Ms Young about how we can work together to resolve this, and we visited her at home this week to agree a way forward".

articles.title: Solar power plans for Northampton's Royal & Derngate theatre
articles.summary: The council hopes to install 232 rooftop solar panels at the same time as fixing a leaky roof.
articles.body:
A town centre theatre could have most of its energy needs met by on-site solar power, if planning permission is granted.

The application for major roof works at the Royal & Derngate theatre in Northampton is being considered by West Northamptonshire Council (WNC).

The council owns the building – but not the theatre business – and hopes to install 232 rooftop solar panels at the same time as fixing a leaky roof.

It comes as a separate £538K project to refurbish the auditorium is under way.

Arts Council England provided the grant to allow for the 43-year-old Derngate building to be upgraded.

Proposals to change the roof were spurred on by "water ingress issues [in] existing felted roof areas" as well as a desire to "improve the sustainability of the building".

The planning application said it hoped adding photovoltaic panels would "contribute to the [building's] own energy demands".

"The array would meet 100% of the energy demands of Royal & Derngate and would result in a reduction of 20,658 kg per year of CO2 emissions," it said.

Although the building is Grade II listed, the application said the works would be confined to the modern section of the Royal & Derngate.

It said its map "suggests that the part of the Royal & Derngate buildings to which the applications relate do not form part of the Grade II listing".

The application was submitted in August and people can submit comments by 22 October. A decision is expected to be made on 9 November.

articles.title: Caleb Flynn's mistress avoided charges despite murder texts as her attorney reveals why
articles.summary: Alleigha Botner's attorney tells why she wasn't charged in Ashley Flynn's murder despite 107,000 messages exchanged with Caleb Flynn during their affair.
articles.body: The attorney for Caleb Flynn's former mistress is pushing back against suspicions that she helped plot the murder of the former "American Idol" contestant's wife, telling Fox News Digital that disturbing messages about wanting Ashley Flynn dead were not evidence that his client took part in the Tipp City, Ohio, killing. Dayton defense attorney Nick Gounaris, who represents Alleigha Botner, said investigators reviewed her messages with Flynn, cellphone records and surveillance footage as they worked to determine whether she had any involvement in the crime. Botner's secret affair with Flynn became a central part of his trial, where jurors heard exchanges about killing his wife, including a suggestion to hire someone to do it. Flynn was ultimately convicted on Sept. 29 of murdering Ashley and sentenced on Monday to life in prison without the possibility of parole. 'AMERICAN IDOL' ALUM CALEB FLYNN WEEPS AS DAUGHTERS ASK HIM WHY HE KILLED THEIR MOTHER, VOW NOT TO VISIT HIM "I think the reason that she wasn't charged is just because you say something, you still have to show that that person was somehow involved," Gounaris told Fox News Digital. "The evidence that was reviewed, the evidence that was developed, the evidence that they secured through all of these different avenues did not suggest anything that involved Alleigha Botner in the death of Ashley Flynn." Gounaris said he initially worried Botner could become a target of the investigation after she spoke to police without an attorney and was not entirely forthcoming about her relationship with Flynn. WATCH: ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ ALUM CALEB FLYNN TELLS COPS FLAG-CARRYING STRANGER CAME TO DOOR BEFORE WIFE’S SHOOTING Investigators had begun uncovering the affair while examining the Feb. 16 shooting at the couple's Tipp City home, where prosecutors said Flynn shot his wife twice in the back of the head before staging a break-in. Botner eventually acknowledged the relationship, but her family became concerned about her legal exposure and contacted Gounaris, who began speaking with investigators to determine whether she was a witness or potential suspect. MISTRESS TOLD ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT SHE WANTED ‘TO KILL’ WIFE BUT TESTIFIED DIVORCE, NOT MURDER, WAS PLAN "As a defense attorney, my first reaction is, wait a minute, we've got to be very careful ... we've got to be concerned that she might be a target here," Gounaris said. "So ... let me bring her into the office. Let's protect her. Let me now be her advocate. Let me speak with investigators and let me then determine, you know, where this is going." As more evidence emerged, Gounaris said, investigators increasingly treated Botner as a witness, and nothing they uncovered suggested she participated in Ashley's murder. DAD OF 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT'S SLAIN WIFE MADE EERIE GOOGLE SEARCH AFTER HEARING OF HER MURDER Jurors heard that Flynn and Botner exchanged over 107,000 messages during their affair, including conversations in which Flynn repeatedly expressed a desire to kill his wife. In one message, Flynn said he had stayed awake thinking of ways to kill Ashley without going to jail. WATCH: Caleb Flynn had ominous response when mistress said ‘I want to kill her’ Gounaris acknowledged the exchanges were ugly but argued that messages discussing Ashley's death represented only a small fraction of their conversations and largely occurred months before the killing. MISTRESS TOLD ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT SHE WANTED ‘TO KILL’ WIFE BUT TESTIFIED DIVORCE, NOT MURDER, WAS PLAN Some of the most troubling exchanges came just hours before Ashley was killed, when Flynn told Botner, "It's happening," and she responded, "You're about to be free." Gounaris said the messages were about Flynn's plans to divorce his wife, explaining that the pair had stopped communicating for roughly a month after Botner ended their relationship in January because Flynn repeatedly failed to leave Ashley. MISTRESS TOLD ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT SHE WANTED ‘TO KILL’ WIFE BUT TESTIFIED DIVORCE, NOT MURDER, WAS PLAN Flynn contacted her again shortly before the murder, claiming he was finally preparing to seek a divorce and disclose the affair to church leadership, Gounaris explained. The renewed conversations included roughly 250 messages discussing divorce, custody, employment and what would happen if Flynn left his marriage, he said. Botner even researched divorce-related questions using ChatGPT and sent Flynn screenshots. MISTRESS TOLD ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT SHE WANTED ‘TO KILL’ WIFE BUT TESTIFIED DIVORCE, NOT MURDER, WAS PLAN "All of the communications that are contemporaneous with the time that he kills his wife all the way up to 12:45 in that morning – about an hour and 45 minutes ... before he calls 911 – are all about divorce," Gounaris said. He maintained that Botner believed Flynn was preparing to leave his wife, not kill her, an explanation she also gave during her testimony. But questions about Botner's conduct extended beyond the messages themselves. During the trial, jurors heard about efforts to conceal the affair, including discussions about deleting communications and replacing phones. Gounaris argued those conversations were motivated by concerns that the relationship could jeopardize Flynn's chances of gaining custody of his daughters during a divorce. "What are they covering up?" Gounaris asked. "They're covering up what the relationship was. So she was explaining to him, 'You need to go get a new phone, you need to delete this app. We ... have not had these conversations.'" FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X The attorney also offered his own theory about why Flynn killed Ashley, suggesting the former church music leader may have realized that ending his marriage would cost him the comfortable life he had built. Flynn worked for his father-in-law's company, had two daughters and held a prominent role at his church. Gounaris believes the prospect of losing those things may have pushed him toward a fatal decision. "He had a girlfriend. He liked having a girlfriend. He had a wife. He liked having his wife, he liked his children, he liked his job, he liked his income, he liked his ... he liked it all," Gounaris said. "On the early morning of Feb. 16, something in his mind said, 'Wait a minute, this is not going to work out for me. I'm not going to have my job. I'm going to be thrown out of the church,' and something happened that caused him to end the life of his wife." CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB "I think it was something that occurred right at that moment at night," he said. "I think that he did things. I think he was sloppy with how he did things." SEND US A TIP That assessment remains the attorney's theory. Jurors convicted Flynn of aggravated murder and eight other counts after roughly 2½ hours in the deliberation room. Flynn continued to maintain his innocence at sentencing, telling the court he did not kill his wife. Flynn's attorneys filed a notice of appeal Wednesday in Miami County court, two days after he was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. GOT A TIP? articles.title: Man with a gun and knife is fatally shot by security at Nashville federal courthouse, police say
articles.summary: NASHVILLE, Tenn. — A man armed with a pistol and knife was fatally shot by a security officer Thursday just inside the busy entrance of a federal courthouse in Tennessee’s largest city, authorities said.
articles.body: NASHVILLE, Tenn. — A man armed with a pistol and knife was fatally shot by a security officer Thursday just inside the busy entrance of a federal courthouse in Tennessee’s largest city, authorities said. The man in his 40s tried to fire his gun but failed and then pulled out a knife at around 9:30 a.m., said Don Aaron, spokesperson for Metro Nashville Police. “The security individual fired on the armed individual,” Aaron said, adding that the man was taken to a hospital where he was pronounced dead. The man was from out of state. Investigators didn’t immediately know why he was at the courthouse, and a search of his car found “nothing threatening,” Aaron said. Courthouse visitors must go through a security checkpoint, which is common at all federal courts. The entrances are typically staffed by armed former police officers contracted by the U.S. Marshals Service. “That’s the entrance that most people in this courthouse use,” First Assistant U.S. Attorney Rob McGuire told reporters outside. The library next door was closed as a result, and officers with dogs were circling the perimeter while workers in nearby buildings gathered to watch. McGuire noted that the local U.S. Attorney’s Office is inside the courthouse, as are the offices of Tennessee’s U.S. senators. There have been “security instances where a person acts up or acts inappropriately and has to be removed from the premises, but nothing even approaching this kind of situation,” he said. Reports of the shooting immediately stirred anxiety and concern. “People are calling their families to let them know they’re OK,” McGuire said. “I called my wife, called my son, called people that I knew were wanting to know if I was OK. We’re all doing that.”

articles.title: Milan US consulate labour 'exploitation' case: Indian workers among hundreds agree to share of $35m payout
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: More than 100 construction workers, most of them from India, are set to receive payouts from a 31-million-euro (nearly $35 million) settlement
articles.body: NEW DELHI: More than 100 construction workers, most of them from India, are set to receive payouts from a 31-million-euro (nearly $35 million) settlement reached with an American construction company over alleged labour exploitation at the site of a new US consulate compound in Milan.Over 60 workers, mostly Indians, signed agreements at a Milan hotel on Wednesday to receive their share of the settlement with Alabama-based Caddell Construction. The signing process began on Tuesday, with 115 workers having signed agreements over two days. The procedure will continue next week, reported Associated press.Prosecutors have described the settlement as the largest ever reached over labour exploitation in Europe. Nearly 480 workers could eventually receive payouts, including about 300 still working at the Milan site, another 100 working elsewhere in Italy and others who have returned to their home countries.The individual payouts average around 45,000 euros (about $50,400), with the highest reaching nearly 90,000 euros (about $101,000), according to Francesco Brigatti, the court-appointed administrator overseeing efforts to bring the construction site into legal compliance.The payments include unpaid overtime, reimbursement for housing costs that were allegedly illegally deducted from workers' wages and damages sought by investigating prosecutor Paolo Storari. Brigatti said the damages component alone accounts for 60-70% of the overtime amount, significantly higher than the 10-30% he said is more customary in such cases.For Dilip Ram, a 43-year-old mason from Bihar who has worked at the Milan consulate site for more than two years, the settlement could make a significant difference to his family back home.“Things are better now than before … we get more rest now,” Ram said after signing the agreement, as quoted by AP, adding, “This has led to a lot of change. This settlement will be good. Because the workers had troubles, that's why this settlement has been applied.”What prosecutors allegedItalian prosecutors allege that workers at the project were paid less than $2 an hour, had money illegally deducted from their wages for accommodation and were denied overtime despite working up to 10 hours a day, six days a week.The workers were also allegedly subjected to threats and did not receive proper medical care after workplace injuries, prosecutors said.Most of the workers were from India, while others came from Nigeria, Kenya and Bangladesh. Indian workers told authorities they had paid recruiters around 5,000 euros (about $5,600) to secure the jobs. However, the settlement does not directly cover alleged abuses in India because Italian prosecutors could not investigate those claims.Each worker signed a document agreeing not to discredit Caddell and not to disclose the amount of their individual payment. Caddell said in the agreement that the settlement did not constitute an admission of liability. Two managers under investigation for alleged extortion and facilitating illegal immigration remain under house arrest.Workers to get Italian work permitsThe settlement also includes about 11.2 million euros $12.5 million) for Italy's social security system and workplace injury insurance.As part of the arrangement, workers will also receive permits allowing them to work in Italy outside the Caddell project.“We have asked the Indian consulate to help,” said Adelio Riva, a labour lawyer working as a consultant for the prosecutor's office. “We are relying heavily on word-of-mouth because, as they say, follow the money.”The three construction-worker trade unions involved in assisting the workers are also monitoring the settlement process.Union organiser Trifone Radogna of Feneal Uil said workers had initially been denied union access at the consulate construction site, with diplomatic status cited as the reason. He said unions had never previously been barred from informing workers of their rights at construction sites in Milan.“We have never encountered a labour-exploitation system on this scale,” Radogna said.“Here workers' dignity was lost: they found themselves without accommodation, without meals, and they were already starting at a disadvantage because they had to pay 5,000 euros before leaving.”Caddell, US government responseCaddell, a major contractor for US embassies and consulates worldwide, said it was cooperating with Italian authorities and reviewing its global subcontractors and consultancies for compliance with labour laws.“Caddell continues to cooperate in good faith with the appropriate authorities throughout this process, and we remain focused on the care and well-being of the people working on an important project,” the company said on Wednesday.The US State Department has said it is investigating the allegations and that US law enforcement agencies are working with Italian authorities. articles.title: In 2023, California shifted a levee 1,500 feet back and flooded fields in winter; the new floodplain produced unexpectedly huge amounts of food for young salmon
articles.summary: In 2023, California's levee setback project unexpectedly enhanced food availability for young salmon in the Yolo Bypass, showcasing a unique blend of flood management and ecological benefits.
articles.body: California completed the main levee setback work on a stretch of the Yolo Bypass near West Sacramento in 2023 and moved the eastern levee roughly 1,500 feet away from the river. The change widened the floodplain and allowed seasonal floodwater to spread across fields that had been separated from the river by levees. Researchers found unexpectedly high concentrations of zooplankton, which are tiny aquatic animals that provide an important food source for juvenile salmon, when winter storms later inundated the expanded area.The project is called the Lower Elkhorn Basin Levee Setback, or LEBLS, and covers about five miles along the Yolo Bypass and another two miles along the Sacramento Bypass. The new setback levee was completed in October 2023, and portions of the old levee were removed as construction progressed. California's Department of Water Resources designed the project with a goal to increase flood capacity and lower water levels in the Sacramento River during major flood events. It also created more seasonal floodplain habitat for fish and wildlife.The fields became a seasonal fish nurseryThe expanded Yolo Bypass floods during periods of high water and then drains as river levels fall, and that cycle is important for juvenile salmon because shallow floodplain water warms more quickly and can support large amounts of aquatic food. DWR scientists expected the newly inundated fields to provide productive habitat, but what they did not expect was how much zooplankton would appear during the first monitoring period. DWR and UC Davis researchers sampled the floodplain in December 2024, after winter storms had filled the bypass. The samples contained large quantities of zooplankton, and subsequent visits found similar results. Researchers continued monitoring the site to determine whether the high food production would persist under different seasonal conditions.UC Davis research has already documented the importance of floodplain food production for young Chinook salmon in the wider Yolo Bypass, where they have found that zooplankton and other organisms can provide the food young salmon need while they grow in seasonally flooded areas, before continuing downstream. UC Davis overview of floodplain research states that juvenile salmon feeding in the Yolo Bypass can show greater growth than fish that remain in the adjacent river channel.A levee project with two jobsThe LEBLS project was built around flood management rather than just salmon, and by moving the levee away from the river, engineers increased the amount of space available for floodwater. DWR says the larger project is intended to improve flood protection for communities around Sacramento and West Sacramento while also increasing the capacity of the Yolo and Sacramento bypasses. The expanded floodplain also gives seasonal water more room to spread across agricultural land instead of remaining confined to the river channel.DWR's project records list more than 1,200 acres of additional bypass storage and floodplain inundation that have been associated with the project, and the agency continues to describe LEBLS as a multi-benefit project that combines flood protection with ecosystem improvements. The early salmon findings do not establish a long-term effect on salmon populations, since researchers are still collecting data on how the floodplain food supply changes across seasons and how juvenile fish use the restored area. The first measurements, however, show that when water reaches the expanded floodplain, the fields can produce substantially more food for young salmon than researchers initially expected.You use AI every day. articles.summary: An attorney for one of the men accused in the alleged Cornell fraternity sexual assault case has asked a New York court to remove Attorney General Letitia
articles.body: An attorney for one of the men accused in the alleged Cornell fraternity sexual assault case has asked a New York court to remove Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor, arguing that her public comments show she may be biased against the accused.Gillio Lopes, one of seven men named in a civil lawsuit filed by a former Cornell University student, submitted a petition in New York State Supreme Court on Wednesday seeking to void James’ appointment or limit her personal involvement in the investigation.His lawyers have also asked New York Governor Kathy Hochul to appoint a different special prosecutor.The former student, identified as Jane Doe in the lawsuit, has alleged that she was drugged and sexually assaulted by members of the Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024. Lopes has dismissed the allegations through his attorney.Lopes’ lawyers are challenging James’ appointment based in part on a statement she posted on the New York attorney general’s official X account days before Hochul appointed her to oversee the case.“What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable,” James wrote, adding that she stood with the alleged victim and “all survivors.”The petition argues that the statement showed James had already formed an opinion about the allegations before conducting an investigation.Lopes’ attorney Andrew Miltenberg claimed James had effectively indicated that she believed the allegations and had reached a conclusion about the accused men’s guilt.Why was James appointed?Hochul appointed James as special prosecutor after saying she had lost confidence in local prosecutors who had previously declined to bring criminal charges in the case.Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten had said his office relied on the investigation conducted by Cornell campus police and explained why charges were not filed in 2024, despite Doe reporting the incident to campus police.Doe later filed a civil complaint in September alleging that she had been drugged with ketamine before being sexually assaulted for several hours at the fraternity house.The complaint also alleges that one of the men sent a Snapchat message to other Chi Phi members referring to the alleged victim.Lopes was suspended by Cornell for three semesters following a university investigation. He has denied the allegations.His lawyers acknowledged that James later said her office would conduct the investigation “fully and fairly” and follow the facts and the law.However, they argued that her earlier public comments still created an appearance of bias.The petition does not seek to stop the investigation. Instead, Lopes’ attorneys want James removed as special prosecutor and a new prosecutor appointed, arguing that the case should be handled by someone without an actual or perceived conflict of interest.You use AI every day. articles.title: Adidas sues Australian label White Fox over four stripes design
articles.summary: The German sportswear brand wants the Sydney-based label to stop selling the clothes and pay damages.
articles.body:
Adidas is suing Australian label White Fox for selling and advertising clothes with a four-striped design, arguing it is "deceptively similar" to the German brand's distinct logo.

The sportswear giant said it had repeatedly asked White Fox to stop selling and promoting the clothes since March, but the Sydney-based company refused.

The fast-fashion online retailer is popular with teenagers and young adults in Australia, the UK and the US, and has relied on billboards, bus advertising and influencers - often university-aged - to grow its profile.

The Australian law firms representing Adidas and White Fox both declined to comment on the case, the first hearing due to begin on Friday.

In Federal Court documents, Adidas states that its three-striped design has a "substantial and valuable reputation" in Australia, where it has been trademarked since 1957.

The company says since at least March, White Fox has been selling and advertising clothes with four parallel stripes of equal width, which it claims is an infringement of Adidas's trademark.

White Fox's designs are "substantially identical with or otherwise deceptively similar" to Adidas, the company claims.

It also argues that White Fox's advertisements for its four-striped clothes and White Fox-branded socks feature people wearing "genuine" Adidas items.

This might lead Australians to think Adidas is associated with White Fox and has approved of the design, the documents claim.

The company says White Fox is "taking advantage" of Adidas's reputation, "drawing an association in the minds of consumers" of the two brands, or at least "sailing close to the wind".

Adidas, which reported €24.8 billion (£21bn; $28bn) in revenue in 2025, is also seeking damages, saying White Fox must pay them the profit from the products plus interest and costs.

Evidence provided by Adidas included side-by-side comparisons of its products with White Fox clothes which include sweatpants and lounge shorts, as well as images of billboards on buses and at bus stops.

In one example, Adidas claimed that an online listing from June 2025 showed a pair of White Fox-branded socks being modelled by someone wearing pink Adidas shoes.

A few days after the court proceedings were lodged last month, the Adidas logo on the shoes were digitally altered to remove one of the stripes, the documents alleged, and a week later, all three stripes were scrubbed from the image.

In 2013, Adidas successfully sued Pacific Brands in Australia for selling shoes with four stripes.

White Fox was launched in 2013 by Georgia and Daniel Contos and is privately-owned by the Greek-Australian couple and Daniel's mother Melina Maceri. It has a growing presence in the US and expanded into the UK market in 2024.

In the 12 months to June 2025, the company generated AU$542m (£286m; $377m) in revenue, a four-fold jump from its 2022 figure of $121m, according to the Australian Financial Review.

articles.title: Walt Disney quietly assembled more than 27,000 acres in Florida through secret transactions for about $5 million, averaging roughly $182 an acre; after the buyer’s identity emerged, the land became Walt Disney World
articles.summary: Walt Disney’s plan for what would become Walt Disney World began with a remarkably quiet real-estate operation.
articles.body: Walt Disney’s plan for what would become Walt Disney World began with a remarkably quiet real-estate operation. According to Disney’s D23 archives, the Florida Historical Society and the Walt Disney Company, Disney Productions spent about 18 months secretly assembling more than 27,000 acres in Central Florida before publicly acknowledging that it was behind the purchases. The operation was designed around a simple concern: If landowners discovered that Disney was buying the property, prices could soar before the company had secured enough acreage.The man tasked with avoiding that outcome was Robert Price “Bob” Foster, a lawyer who had joined Walt Disney Productions after working on Disneyland. In late 1963, Walt and his brother Roy Disney selected Foster to lead the Florida land acquisition effort, which was internally known as “Project X.” Foster initially expected to acquire somewhere between 5,000 and 10,000 acres. Instead, the project ultimately grew into a massive 43-square-mile land assembly.Beginning in 1964, Disney representatives purchased properties through a collection of seemingly unrelated companies. Florida Memory identifies nine front companies used in the acquisitions, including Latin-American Development & Management Corporation and Reedy Creek Ranch Inc. The strategy helped keep the true buyer hidden while parcels were accumulated across parts of Orange and Osceola counties.Foster himself operated under the name “Bob Price” while working on the acquisitions. D23 says he negotiated with more than 100 landowners and helped assemble more than 27,000 acres, including property around Bay Lake and what became Discovery Island. The final purchase covered roughly 27,443 acres. Disney has described the acquisition as costing about $5 million, with an average price of less than $200 an acre. Other historical accounts put the average at approximately $182 to $185 per acre, depending on the transaction figures used.At the time, however, Central Florida did not look like the destination it would eventually become. Much of the property consisted of undeveloped land, swamps, forests and agricultural acreage. Disney had chosen the region partly because its inland location reduced exposure to coastal hurricanes and offered the company an opportunity to build something much larger than Disneyland.The secrecy eventually became impossible to maintain. Local reporters had begun investigating the mysterious purchases as thousands of acres changed hands. In October 1965, Orlando Sentinel reporter Emily Bavar publicly connected the land-buying operation to Disney after questioning Walt Disney during a visit to the company’s California studio. The Sentinel subsequently identified Disney as the mystery buyer, ending the operation’s biggest secret.The following month, Walt and Roy Disney appeared alongside Florida Gov. Haydon Burns at a press conference in Orlando and formally announced the Florida Project. Disney revealed plans for a huge new destination that would go far beyond a traditional theme park. Walt Disney would not live to see the project completed. He died in December 1966, while construction was still underway. But the enormous property he had helped secure gave the company something Disneyland never had: room to expand on an extraordinary scale.The Magic Kingdom eventually opened on October 1, 1971, transforming the former Central Florida acreage into the foundation of Walt Disney World. The land deal also became the beginning of a larger experiment in development and governance. Foster helped establish the legal framework that eventually created the Reedy Creek Improvement District, allowing Disney to manage infrastructure and services across much of the property.What started with a handful of secretive land purchases therefore became one of the most consequential real-estate moves in American entertainment history. Disney did not simply buy land for another theme park. It quietly acquired enough territory to build an entire vacation destination on its own terms.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Ithaca city council calls on Cornell to report sexual assault investigations to local police
articles.summary: The city of Ithaca called on the Cornell University Police Department to turn over sex and violent crime investigations to the Ithaca Police Department, after the city council voted nearly unanimously in favor of the measure.
articles.body: The city of Ithaca called on the Cornell University Police Department to turn over sex and violent crime investigations to the Ithaca Police Department, after the city council voted nearly unanimously in favor of the measure. The decision late Wednesday came as a gang-rape allegation by a former Cornell student took the campus and nation by storm last month. The Cornell University Police Department has said it did not refer its investigation of the 2024 allegation to the Ithaca Police Department. The former student, known as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit last month detailing the allegations and what she said was a lack of appropriate response by the university and its police department. The city council also voted on Wednesday to temporarily suspend affiliated student organizations at the university, such as fraternities, from new assemblies, parades and special events “due to public safety concerns.” The moratorium on events would expire on Nov. 5, unless the council were to take further action, according to a meeting agenda. The resolution passed by a vote of 9-1. The council did not say how the measure would be enforced or what would happen if the university did not comply. Cornell declined to comment, citing pending litigation. More than 35% of female undergraduates surveyed at Cornell University reported experiencing nonconsensual sexual contact involving physical force, threats of force or incapacitation, according to a poll conducted last year. That figure was up from 23% in 2023, according to the university. The university police department and the local district attorney are under intense scrutiny over how the investigation into Doe’s allegations was handled. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten previously said he based his decision not to bring charges based on a six-page summary made by Cornell police of Jane Doe’s initial interview with police. But, according to reports, that summary was missing some of Jane Doe’s strongest remarks to police. CBS News New York, citing a transcript of a conversation between Jane Doe and investigators, reported that she told campus police three weeks after the fraternity incident that she had been raped. “I can say with 100% confidence I was raped,” Jane Doe is quoted as saying. Van Houten said he was unaware that Jane Doe allegedly made that remark to campus police, adding that the allegation was not included in the written statement that Cornell police provided to his office in November 2024. In light of the revelations, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said, “In what world would the police learn from a victim that she’d been literally gang-raped while intoxicated by five men in a fraternity house, and not elevate those allegations to the district attorney?” “She spoke to the police. She sat for hours and told them exactly what happened to her and according to new reports, she could not have been clearer that she was 100% confident that she had been raped,” she said. “Yet, shockingly, those words never made it into the account that the Cornell police sent to prosecutors. The attorney general then declined to pursue charges after reviewing that incomplete account and never interviewing her.” Hochul has appointed Attorney General Letitia James to take over the investigation. As governor of New York, Hochul is by default a member of the board of trustees at Cornell. Jane Doe’s attorney has argued that she was failed by authorities who did not conduct a thorough investigation. Sally Yates, the former deputy U.S. attorney general and acting U.S. attorney general, is leading an independent review of how the university responded to the allegations and, more broadly, how it responds to sexual harassment, assault and misconduct on campus. That probe will include looking into the role and response of campus police and its coordination with other law enforcement agencies and prosecutors. If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at rainn.org/get-help.

articles.title: San Diego restaurant staff stunned to find out chef of 10 years was an Iowa fugitive using alias
articles.summary: A San Diego chef was arrested this week on allegations that he’s spent the past 14 years on the run after fleeing Iowa, where he was facing prosecution for the alleged kidnapping, assault and shooting of a woman.
articles.body: A San Diego chef was arrested this week on allegations that he’s spent the past 14 years on the run after fleeing Iowa, where he was facing prosecution for the alleged kidnapping, assault and shooting of a woman. Brian Anthony Williams, 50, who has been working as a chef under the name “Troy Williams,” according to the U.S. Marshals Service, was charged in 2012 in Iowa’s Scott County, where he and co-conspirators allegedly kidnapped, assaulted and shot a woman, then left her in a field. Williams has been working as head chef of Miss B’s Coconut Club in Mission Beach for about 10 years. Williams allegedly fled Iowa to avoid prosecution, but the U.S. Marshals Service said it later learned he was living in San Diego and had appeared in local print and television news stories as Troy Williams. Williams was arrested Tuesday at Miss B’s Coconut Club and is awaiting extradition to Iowa, where he faces charges of first-degree kidnapping, assault, conspiracy to commit a felony and first-degree arson. He also faces charges of unlawful flight for allegedly fleeing Iowa. His colleagues were in utter shock and disbelief to learn that Williams was a fugitive. NBC San Diego spoke with the restaurant’s general manager, Eddie Jurado, who said he was still processing everything that had just transpired. Jurado was stunned when a friend called to inform him of Williams’ arrest at work on Tuesday morning. Jurado spoke with an investigator on the phone about the situation. “He’s like, Troy is not coming back. I’m like, What? He’s like Google ‘Brian Anthony Williams.’ He couldn’t say anything. So I’m like, OK,” Jurado said. Jurado knew him really well — or at least thought he did. Jurado did indeed Google “Brian Anthony Williams” and a mug shot of his head chef came up. “This is crazy, we’ve been through it. I’ve been here 10½ years, he’s been here 10½ years. He’s been running that kitchen for about eight or nine, once our first chef left and he took it over. We’ve been through Covid. I was his roommate for a while and he’s not even Troy,” Jurado said. Jurado said he and his colleagues still can’t wrap their minds around how Williams managed to live under a different identity for as long as he did. Employees feel very sorry for the victim and what she went through, Jurado said. As of Wednesday, it is not yet known when Williams will be extradited to Iowa.

articles.title: Flood crisis persists; residents struggle for food, water and shelter
articles.summary: Lucknow Gomti floods disrupt life for 10 days; 40,000 homes hit in Faizullaganj, relief underway, IIIT-L closed, river may recede in 24 hours.
articles.body: Lucknow: For 10 days, 45-year-old daily-wage worker Yasmeen Bano has been living with her family on the rooftop of their home in Faizullaganj after floodwater submerged the ground floor and damaged their gas cooktop. Her daughter has developed flu-like symptoms, forcing the family to travel by boat to get medicines.“We have a single-storey house and are living on the rooftop, exposed to the scorching sun during the day and dew at night. With my two daughters, even meeting our basic needs has become difficult. We struggle to use the toilet, bathe, get food on time and maintain a healthy routine,” she said.Yasmeen is among thousands of residents affected by flooding in Faizullaganj and other low-lying areas as Gomti continues to rise. Officials said around 40,000 houses across several colonies in Faizullaganj have been affected, with water reaching 4-6ft inside some homes. Phoenix Palassio mall has effectively become an island, while water has also reached Ekana Stadium and the disaster management office.The flooding has forced many families to leave their homes or move to upper floors. In Millatnagar, Suresh Awasthi shifted his family to his village after floodwaters disrupted daily life.“I have shifted my family to my village as I have no one here in the city. My children’s studies have been affected and I have not been able to assess the loss of my belongings,” he said.Residents, who remain in flooded localities, said access to food and drinking water has become difficult, with many dependent on relief supplies.“We cannot go out whenever we need water or food. We have to depend on people who come here with relief material,” a resident said.Waterlogging has also created sanitation problems.“There is water everywhere and it has become difficult to use toilets. We are worried about the hygiene of our children,” said Deepu, a resident of Mama Colony.Boat travel has become the main mode of transport in several areas.“The boats deployed in the area charge Rs 100-200 per trip. We have to pay just to commute,” said Rakesh Yadav of Daudnagar.The flooding has also hit livelihoods. Shops remain shut in several localities and daily-wage workers have lost income.Ravi Gupta, who runs a grocery shop, said his business has remained closed for 10 days.Educational institutions have also been affected.IIIT-Lucknow will remain closed till Sunday after large parts of its campus were inundated. Examinations have been postponed and electricity supply was switched off as a safety measure. Around 800 hostellers were evacuated, with 300 returning home and the remaining shifted to alternative accommodation.Dean Deepak Kumar Singh said floodwaters entered the campus on Wednesday morning and continued to rise, prompting the institute to inform local authorities. Following a joint inspection by the SDM and tehsildar, it was decided to shut the campus till Sunday.“The situation will be reviewed after Sunday before a decision is taken on reopening. Electricity has been switched off as a safety measure and classes may be held online if required,” Singh said.Gomti Likely to Recede Within 24 HoursGomti’s water level is falling upstream and is expected to decline in the city within 24 hours, a senior irrigation department official said on Thursday.At Naimisharanya, the river level dropped by 46cm to 121.56m, while at Bhatpurwa it fell to 113.03m. In the city, the level stood at 108.60m at Gaughat, 107.29m at Hanuman Setu and 107.03m at Gomti Barrage.The official said the falling level at Itaunja is also expected to impact the city. Floodplain work will begin once water recedes and affected areas become accessible. He added that while LDA has cleared development from Pakka Pul up to the road stretch, further work will require surveys.Mayor Reviews Relief MeasuresMayor Sushma Kharkwal on Thursday visited flood-hit areas including Lohramau, Faizullaganj, Daud Nagar, Millat Nagar, Hayat Nagar, Gulmi Kheda, reaching some locations by boat. She met affected residents, distributed food packets, drinking water and medicines, and directed officials to ensure uninterrupted relief supplies. Kharkwal also inspected a health camp, reviewed medical services and medicine availability, and asked health workers to provide timely treatment to residents. Later, she reviewed operations at the flood relief control room and directed officials to address all complaints promptly. The mayor also checked the quality of food being served to flood victims and instructed officials to distribute food packets three times a day.LDA Intensifies Drainage OperationsLDA has intensified drainage and relief work around Ekana Stadium and Phoenix Palassio Mall, where waterlogging has occurred due to the rising Gomti. Officials said they created a temporary embankment of boulders and soil to prevent river water from entering the area, while 26 pumping sets are being used to drain out water.LDA vice-chairperson Prathamesh Kumar and secretary Sushil Pratap Singh inspected the affected sites and directed officials to expedite relief measures. articles.summary: The benefits of a quality humidifier include moisturizing skin, fighting off allergens and even defending against dry lips and mouth, according to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
articles.body: The benefits of a quality humidifier include moisturizing skin, fighting off allergens and even defending against dry lips and mouth, according to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). If you use one often, then knowing how to clean and maintain your humidifier regularly will ensure that it doesn’t grow mold and present health risks in the future. I spoke with cleaning experts for their cleaning guidance and product recommendations. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Why do humidifiers need to be cleaned? Since the inside of a humidifier contains stagnant water of varying temperatures and little ventilation, it’s susceptible to growing residue. “The biggest issues with humidifiers are the build-up of a slimy film in the reservoir, potential bacteria and mold growth, and mineral build-up,” says Melissa Maker, author and founder of cleaning site Clean My Space. “All of which can be pumped into the air you breathe.” Additionally, how you clean your humidifier may depend on the type, such as ultrasonic, steam, evaporative or impeller, which we explain more in our roundup of the best humidifiers. Plus, it’s important to clean your humidifier so that you can actually benefit from using it, says Delah Gomasi, founder of Maid For You. “One of the things that hinders its performance is scale (mineral deposit) buildup which clogs pretty much everything from the misting plate and water reservoir to the filter and crevices within the machine,” he says. “Simply put, when scale buildup prevents misting, there is no humidification taking place.” How to clean a humidifier Unplug the humidifier and let it sit for a few minutes if it’s warm to the touch.Pour out any water sitting in the tank and use a paper towel to wipe away any visible “slime” or residue. Remove all detachable parts, such as the water tank. If you’re cleaning an evaporative humidifier, this includes the filter inside. Soak a paper towel in warm soapy water and wring out the excess water. Wipe the inside of the water tank clean. Alternatively, use a sprayable dish soap, such as Dawn Platinum Powerwash Dish Spray, to lightly coat the inside of the tank. Use a moist paper towel to wipe it clean.Add equal parts white vinegar and water to the tank and let it sit for 30 minutes. This will help get rid of any odors or remaining residue. Pour out the mixture. Rinse the tank, let it dry completely and then add clean water when you’re ready to use it again. These reusable, absorbent cleaning cloths are well suited for many tasks, including cleaning the inside and outside of a humidifier. Plus, they’re machine washable. Hydrogen peroxide isn’t just for first aid purposes — it’s also great for household cleaning. This food-grade option is safe to use around the inside of your humidifier. Add some to a cloth or put some in a spray bottle to apply all over. Hydrogen peroxide has similar properties to bleach, but with much less toxicity, particularly at a low concentration. This absorbent paper humidifier filter replacement is compatible with most Honeywell humidifiers. It traps dust, pet dander, dirt and other particles, while also helping your humidifier to release fresh moisture into the air, according to the brand. This solution helps remove mineral deposits that typically build up in humidifiers filled with hard water. If you use tap water in your coffee makers or pots, you can use this descaler to clean those appliances too, according to the brand. Tips for cleaning different types of humidifiers Since there are humidifiers that create mists in different ways (such as cool-mist and warm mists) some of them have parts that need to be cleaned that others don’t. Plus, some humidifiers require replacement filters. Evaporative humidifiers: These types of humidifiers have an internal filter, such as a wick filter (mesh-like filter that resembles a sponge). If your humidifier’s filter is reusable and relatively new, you can clean it by soaking it in vinegar and water for 30 minutes. Then, use a nylon bristle brush to scrub off any residue. Let dry before replacing. If your humidifier has a wick filter, it’s best to replace it with a new one, such as the Durabasics Premium Humidifier Filter, and buy multi-packs of them.Ultrasonic/impeller humidifiers: An ultrasonic humidifier, which doesn’t have a filter, uses ultrasonic vibrations to release water into the air. Maker recommends focusing on descaling the inside, especially if you use hard unfiltered water with a lot of mineral deposits for your humidifier. The Durgol Universal Multipurpose Descaler can help remove any scaling in your humidifier. Steam vaporizers: This is a type of warm-mist humidifier that uses heat to create steam. Remove the water tank and use warm soapy water and/or a vinegar soak to clean it. articles.title: HC reserves verdict on journalist’s plea challenging NSA detention
articles.summary: Allahabad High Court reserves verdict on journalist Satyam Verma’s plea challenging NSA detention over alleged April 2026 Noida protest role, seeks release.
articles.body: Prayagraj: The Allahabad High Court on Thursday reserved its judgment on a habeas corpus petition filed by journalist Satyam Verma, challenging his preventive detention under the National Security Act (NSA), 1980, in connection with his alleged role in the April 2026 workers’ protest in Noida.A division bench comprising Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev reserved the verdict after hearing the parties over two days, on Oct 7 and 8.Verma has challenged the detention order dated May 12, 2026, issued by the Gautam Budh Nagar district magistrate under the NSA.The petition seeks quashing of the detention order and related proceedings, besides seeking Verma’s immediate release and compensation for his alleged illegal detention.The principal ground raised in the plea is that the detention order was based on a factually untenable premise that Verma was involved in violence in Noida on April 13, 2026.According to the petition, CCTV footage and call detail records (CDRs) show that Verma was nearly 500 km away in Lucknow, where he was allegedly detained by Hasanganj Police at 2:14 pm on the same day. The plea describes this as an “ironclad alibi” and argues that an NSA detention order based on physically impossible and demonstrably false facts is liable to be quashed.The petition further alleges that the investigating officer suppressed the CDRs and CCTV footage from Hasanganj Police Station while placing material before the detaining authority, thereby vitiating its subjective satisfaction.It also contends that Verma was not named in any of the 11 FIRs relied upon by the State to justify the detention.According to the plea, the detention order is based on statements allegedly made by a co-accused or witness, Mangal, while in police custody. The petitioner argues that such statements are inadmissible in law.The petition also disputes the State’s characterisation of Verma’s professional income as funding for riots. It states that his income over nearly two decades was earned through his profession, received through formal banking channels, and disclosed in income tax returns.Another ground raised in the petition is that the material relied upon by the authorities, even if accepted in its entirety, relates to a local labour dispute over minimum wages. According to Verma, such a dispute falls within the ambit of “law and order” and does not constitute a threat to “public order”.The plea alleges that the NSA was used to suppress a spontaneous and lawful labour demand.Stay updated with the latest Prayagraj news. articles.title: India’s Cockroach movement says members detained as protests continue
articles.summary: India’s opposition and student-led CJP movement demand election chief’s resignation, plan mass demonstration Saturday.
articles.body:
India’s Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) says that authorities have detained many of its members as thousands of the group’s supporters and members of several student groups continue to protest, demanding the election chief’s resignation.

Thursday’s demonstrations come ahead of CJP-led antigovernment protests planned for Saturday, with thousands expected to march to Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in the capital, New Delhi.

Ashutosh Ranka, a spokesperson for the movement, said in a post on X on Thursday that “at least 10,000” people from CJP demonstrations, student organisations, affiliated grassroots groups and political parties had been detained across the country.

Among those arrested is CJP national spokesman Deepak Baliyan, who was taken into police custody on Thursday, according to the group’s statements.

Al Jazeera could not immediately verify the claims, but videos posted on X showed activists being taken away in vans.

Opposition parties and students affiliated with the CJP movement have been demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, over a controversial revision of voter lists.

They accuse the poll body he heads of benefitting Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

On Thursday, CJP said that among those detained was ‌a group of students from the city of Pune who were headed for New Delhi to participate in planned protests at the iconic Jantar Mantar observatory. CJP said they were taken away in a bus to an unknown location.

“Why not just declare EMERGENCY?” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in a response to a post with a video of activists being detained.

India’s Election Commission has so far removed more than 130 million names from the voter lists, with millions appealing the removals. About 969 million people were eligible to vote in the 2024 election.

Protesters allege the changes disproportionately removed voters who support opposition parties while preserving or adding voters more likely to back Modi’s party.

The commission and government deny the allegations. They say the revision has no political motive but is aimed at removing duplicate and ineligible entries while ensuring eligible voters remain registered.

Earlier on Thursday, thousands of supporters of the CJP youth movement protested in the tech hub of Bengaluru.

Many of the protesters held posters that said, “Every name counts, Every vote matters” and “Stop the Murder of ⁠Democracy”.

Khushi Shrivastava, a 22-year-old architecture student at the protest, told the Reuters news agency: “I think voting right is the most basic point of democracy … People ⁠who actually want to vote, who actually care about the future of India, they are just being [denied] voting rights.”

On Wednesday, Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi was briefly detained for the third time in two days, as his Congress ‌Party accused police of using “brute force”.

Police said the allegations were being used to “defame” them. BJP’s spokesperson ‌Gaurav ‌Bhatia said the allegations were “being levelled by an irresponsible, anarchist opposition”.
